title.zh: 卷四百十一 列傳第一百七十 湯璹 蔣重珍 牟子才 朱貔孫 歐陽守道
title.en: Volume 411 Biographies 170: Tang Shu, Jiang Zhongzhen, Mou Zicai, Zhu Pisun, Ouyang Shoudao
title.raw: 卷四百十一 列傳第一百七十 湯璹 蔣重珍 牟子才 朱貔孫 歐陽守道 Volume 411 Biographies 170: Tang Shu, Jiang Zhongzhen, Mou Zicai, Zhu Pisun, Ouyang Shoudao

sentences.zh: 湯璹 蔣重珍 牟子才 朱貔孫 歐陽守道

translations.literal: Tang Shu, Jiang Zhongzhen, Mou Zicai, Zhu Pisun, Ouyang Shoudao
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shu, Jiang Zhongzhen, Mou Zicai, Zhu Pisun, and Ouyang Shoudao

sentences.zh: 湯璹，字君保，瀏陽人。

translations.literal: Tang Shu, styled Junbao, was a native of Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shu, whose style name was Junbao, came from Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年進士，調徳安府學教授，轉三省樞密院架閣，遷國子博士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fourteenth year of Chunxi, he was assigned professor at the De'an Prefecture school, transferred to archive clerk for the Three Departments and Privy Council, and was promoted to doctor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Chunxi (1187), was assigned as professor at the De'an Prefecture school, transferred to oversee the Three Departments and Privy Council archives, and was promoted to doctor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時召朱熹為侍講，未幾辭歸，朝廷從其請，予祠，璹上疏言：「熹以正學為講官，四方顒望，其有啓沃之益；

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Xi was summoned as court lecturer; before long he requested leave and returned home, and the court granted his request and gave him a temple appointment. Shu submitted a memorial saying, "Xi, as lecturer of orthodox learning, was looked to with hope throughout the realm and would have the benefit of nourishing counsel;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Xi was summoned as court lecturer. Before long he asked to leave and return home, and the court granted his request and gave him a temple appointment. Shu submitted a memorial saying, "Xi, serving as lecturer on orthodox learning, was eagerly awaited throughout the realm and would have benefited the throne through loyal counsel;

sentences.zh: 曾未踰時，輙聴其去，必駭物論，宜追召熹還，仍授講職。」

translations.literal: before much time had passed he was allowed to leave, which will surely shock public opinion; Xi should be urgently recalled and again granted lecturing duties."
translations.idiomatic: yet before much time had passed he was allowed to go, which will surely alarm public opinion. Xi should be urgently recalled and again given his lecturing post."

sentences.zh: 疏上不報，由是浸惡權相意，而璹之直聲亦大聞於時。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and received no response; from this he gradually incurred the displeasure of the chief minister in power, and Shu's reputation for upright speech also became widely known at the time.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered. From then on he gradually fell afoul of the chief minister in power, while Shu's reputation for outspoken integrity became widely known.

sentences.zh: 歴禮部、駕部二郎官，出知常州，入為大理少卿，進直徽猷閣，卒。

translations.literal: He served successively as second-rank bureau officer in the Ministries of Rites and Transport, went out as prefect of Changzhou, entered as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to Direct Huixian Pavilion, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice bureau director in the Ministries of Rites and Transport, was appointed prefect of Changzhou, returned as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to Direct Huixian Pavilion, and died.

sentences.zh: 璹負直槩，與韓侂胄、陳自強不合，故屢嗾言者中傷。

translations.literal: Shu possessed upright character; he did not get along with Han Tuozhou and Chen Ziqiang, and so they repeatedly instigated critics to slander him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was a man of upright character who clashed with Han Tuozhou and Chen Ziqiang, and they repeatedly instigated memorialists to attack him.

sentences.zh: 璹生平奉祠閒居之日多於揚歴，其在禮曹，例掌三省奏記，臨安大火，寧宗遇災，避正殿，中書三表請復，不許，璹屬辭，務持大體，不為阿曲，言者摭其語涉訕上，而朝廷實知其無他，故起復制詞有「清風峻節」之語。

translations.literal: In his life the days Shu spent on temple appointments and in retirement were more than those in official promotion; when he was in the Ministry of Rites section, by precedent he handled memorials for the Three Departments. When a great fire broke out in Lin'an, Emperor Ningzong met with disaster and avoided the main hall; the Secretariat submitted three memorials requesting resumption, but this was not granted. Shu drafted the wording, striving to uphold the larger principles and not to flatter and bend; critics seized upon his language as involving slander of the sovereign, yet the court in fact knew he had no other intent, and so the edict text for resumption contained the phrase "clear wind and lofty integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Shu spent more days on temple appointments and in retirement than in active office. While serving in the Ministry of Rites, he routinely handled memorials for the Three Departments. When a great fire ravaged Lin'an, Emperor Ningzong, responding to the calamity, avoided the main hall. The Secretariat submitted three memorials asking him to resume normal court, but permission was denied. Shu drafted the response, striving to uphold proper principle rather than flatter and compromise. Critics picked out his wording as slanderous of the sovereign, but the court knew he meant no harm, and the edict for the eventual resumption included the phrase "clear wind and lofty integrity."

sentences.zh: 璹嘗擇壻，得蔣重珍，後舉進士第一。

translations.literal: Shu once chose a son-in-law and obtained Jiang Zhongzhen, who later placed first in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shu once chose a son-in-law in Jiang Zhongzhen, who later placed first in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 蔣重珍，字良貴，無錫人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongzhen, styled Lianggui, was a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongzhen, styled Lianggui, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十六年進士第一，簽判建康軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiading he ranked first in the jinshi examination and was appointed signing clerk of Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Jiading (1223) he finished first in the jinshi examination and was appointed signing clerk of Jiankang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，改昭慶軍，尋以公事，與部使者異議，請祠，易簽判奉國軍。

translations.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning and was reassigned to Zhaoqing Prefecture; soon, over official business, he differed with the circuit intendant, requested a temple sinecure, and was transferred to signing clerk of Fengguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he went into mourning and was reassigned to Zhaoqing Prefecture. Soon, over official business, he clashed with the circuit intendant, requested a temple sinecure, and was moved to signing clerk of Fengguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年，召入對，首以自天子至於庶人所當先知者，本心、外物二者之界限為言，界限明，則知有天下治亂而已，何樂其尊；

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoding he was summoned for an imperial audience and began by speaking on what from the Son of Heaven down to commoners ought first to know—the boundary between one's inner mind and external things. Once that boundary is clear, one knows only whether the realm is governed or in disorder—what pleasure is there in rank?
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoding (1229) he was summoned for an imperial audience and began by speaking on what everyone from the Son of Heaven down to commoners ought first to know—the boundary between one's inner mind and external things. Once that boundary is clear, one knows only whether the realm is governed or in disorder—what pleasure is there in rank?

sentences.zh: 知有生民休戚而已，何樂其奉。

translations.literal: One knows only whether the living people are secure or afflicted—what pleasure is there in emolument?
translations.idiomatic: One knows only whether the people are secure or afflicted—what pleasure is there in salary and perquisites?

sentences.zh: 且論：「苞苴有昔所未有之物，故吾民罹昔所未有之害；

translations.literal: And he argued: "When gift-giving has things never seen before, our people suffer harms never seen before;
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "When bribery brings things never seen before, our people suffer harms never seen before;

sentences.zh: 苞苴有不可勝窮之費，故吾民有不可勝窮之憂。」

translations.literal: when gift-giving has expenses that cannot be fully exhausted, our people have worries that cannot be fully exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: when bribery brings expenses that cannot be exhausted, our people have worries that cannot be exhausted."

sentences.zh: 遷祕書省正字，屢乞祠，以伯父䘮，予告，遷校書郎，辭，不可。

translations.literal: He was promoted to rectifier of the Secretariat, repeatedly begged for a temple sinecure; when his paternal uncle died he was granted leave, then promoted to collator—he declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to rectifier in the Secretariat and repeatedly asked for a temple sinecure. When his paternal uncle died he was granted leave, then promoted to collator; he declined, but the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 明年，待命霅川，移文閣門請對，當路憚之，添差通判鎮江府，辭，會行都火，應詔曰：「臣頃進本心外物界限之說，蓋欲陛下親攬大柄，不退託於人，盡破恩私，求無愧於己。

translations.literal: The next year, awaiting appointment at Shechuan, he sent a note through the Gate of Imperial Audience requesting an audience; those in power feared him and appointed him additionally as vice prefect of Zhenjiang Prefecture—he declined. When the traveling capital caught fire, he responded to the imperial edict: "Your servant recently submitted the doctrine of the boundary between inner mind and external things, intending that Your Majesty personally seize the great handle of power, not defer and entrust it to others, utterly break favoritism and private interest, and seek to be without self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, awaiting appointment at Shechuan, he sent a note through the Gate of Imperial Audience requesting an audience. Those in power feared him and gave him additional duty as vice prefect of Zhenjiang; he declined. When the traveling capital caught fire, he responded to the imperial edict: "Your servant recently submitted the doctrine of the boundary between inner mind and external things, intending that Your Majesty personally seize the great handle of power, not defer it to others, utterly break favoritism and private interest, and seek to be without self-reproach.

sentences.zh: 儻以富貴之私視之，一言一動，不忘其私，則是以天下生靈、社稷宗廟之事為輕；

translations.literal: If one views it through the lens of private interest in wealth and rank, and in every word and act does not forget one's private interest, then one treats the affairs of the people under Heaven, the altars of state and the ancestral temples, as light matters;
translations.idiomatic: If one views it through the lens of private interest in wealth and rank, and in every word and act does not forget one's private interest, then one treats the lives of the people, the altars of state, and the ancestral temples as light matters;

sentences.zh: 而以一身富貴之所從來為重，不惟上負天命與先帝、聖母至于公卿百執事之所以望陛下者，亦不如此也。

translations.literal: and treats as weighty matters the sources of one's own personal wealth and rank—not only failing Heaven's mandate and the late emperor and empress dowager, but also failing what from the high ministers down to the hundred officers hoped Your Majesty would be like.
translations.idiomatic: and treats as weighty matters the sources of one's own personal wealth and rank—not only failing Heaven's mandate, the late emperor, and the empress dowager, but also failing what the high ministers and the hundred officers hoped Your Majesty would be.

sentences.zh: 昔周勃今日握璽授文帝，是夜即以宋昌領南北軍；

translations.literal: In former times Zhou Bo that day held the seal and invested Emperor Wen, and that very night Song Chang took command of the northern and southern armies;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Zhou Bo that day held the seal and invested Emperor Wen, and that very night Song Chang took command of the northern and southern armies;

sentences.zh: 霍光今年定䇿立宣帝，而明年稽首歸政。

translations.literal: Huo Guang that year decided the succession and established Emperor Xuan, and the next year bowed his head and returned authority.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang that year decided the succession and established Emperor Xuan, and the next year bowed his head and returned authority.

sentences.zh: 今臨御八年，未聞有所作為，進退人才，興廢政事，天下皆曰：『此丞相意』，一時恩怨，雖歸廟堂，異日治亂，實在陛下焉。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has reigned eight years, yet none has heard of any accomplishment; promotion and dismissal of talent, rise and fall of policies—all under Heaven say: 'This is the chief minister's will.' Present resentments and debts may rest with the court, but future order and disorder truly lie with Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has reigned eight years, yet none has heard of any accomplishment. Promotion and dismissal of talent, rise and fall of policies—all under Heaven say, 'This is the chief minister's will.' Present resentments and debts may rest with the court, but future order and disorder truly lie with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 有為天之子，為人之主，而自朝廷達於天下皆言相而不言君哉？

translations.literal: Can one who is Heaven's son and lord of men have from the court down to all under Heaven everyone speak of the minister and none speak of the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Can one who is Heaven's son and lord of men have everyone from the court down to all under Heaven speak of the minister and none speak of the ruler?

sentences.zh: 天之所以火宗廟、火都城者，殆以此。

translations.literal: Heaven's reason for burning the ancestral temples and burning the capital is probably this.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's reason for burning the ancestral temples and the capital is probably this.

sentences.zh: 臣所以痛心者，九廟至重，事如生存，而徹小塗大，不防於火之未至，宰相之居，華屋廣袤，而焦頭爛額獨全於火之未然，亦足以見人心䧟溺，知有權勢，不知有君父矣！

translations.literal: What moves Your servant to heartbreak is this: the Nine Temples are supremely weighty, treated as though for a living emperor, yet petty matters were pursued while great ones were neglected, with no guard against fire before it came. The chief minister's residence—splendid halls, vast and wide—alone was wholly preserved beforehand, even as others scorched their heads and blistered their brows. This alone suffices to show people's hearts sunk and drowned—knowing power and position, not knowing ruler and father!
translations.idiomatic: What moves your servant to heartbreak is this: the Nine Temples are supremely weighty, tended as though for a living emperor—yet petty matters were pursued while great ones were neglected, with no guard before fire came. The chief minister's residence—splendid halls, vast grounds—alone was wholly spared beforehand, even as others scorched their heads and blistered their brows. This alone suffices to show hearts sunk and drowned: knowing power and position, not knowing ruler and father!

sentences.zh: 他有變故，何所倚仗？

translations.literal: If other crises arise, on whom will Your Majesty rely?
translations.idiomatic: If other crises arise, on whom will Your Majesty rely?

sentences.zh: 陛下自視，不亦孤乎！

translations.literal: When Your Majesty looks at yourself, are you not indeed isolated!
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty looks at yourself, are you not indeed isolated!

sentences.zh: 昔史浩兩入相，才五月，或九月即罷，孝宗之報功，寧有窮已，顧如此其亟，何哉？

translations.literal: In former times Shi Hao entered the chancellorship twice—for only five months, or nine months, before being dismissed. Emperor Xiaozong's reward for merit—could it ever be exhausted? Yet he was removed so quickly—why?
translations.idiomatic: In former times Shi Hao entered the chancellorship twice—for only five months, or nine months, before being dismissed. Emperor Xiaozong's reward for merit—could it ever be exhausted? Yet he was removed so quickly—why?

sentences.zh: 保全功臣之道，可厚以富貴，不可久以權也。」

translations.literal: The way to preserve meritorious ministers is to enrich them with wealth and rank, not to let them hold power for long."
translations.idiomatic: The way to preserve meritorious ministers is to enrich them with wealth and rank, not to let them hold power for long."

sentences.zh: 上讀之感動，授寳章閣，主管雲臺觀，則告吏部，不受貼職祿，不願貼職恩。

translations.literal: The emperor, moved on reading it, granted him Baozhang Pavilion and put him in charge of Yuntai Abbey; he then informed the Ministry of Personnel that he would not accept stipend for the added appointment nor wish for the added appointment's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved on reading it, granted him Baozhang Pavilion and put him in charge of Yuntai Abbey. He then informed the Ministry of Personnel that he would not accept stipend for the added appointment nor wish for its favor.

sentences.zh: 它日，星變求言，復申前說。

translations.literal: Another day, when a stellar anomaly prompted requests for counsel, he again pressed his earlier doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, when a stellar anomaly prompted requests for counsel, he again pressed his earlier doctrine.

sentences.zh: 又慮柄臣或果去位，君心易縱，大權旁落，則進《為君難》六箴。

translations.literal: Also fearing that if the powerful minister truly left office the ruler's heart might easily grow lax and great power slip aside, he submitted the six admonitions entitled "The Difficulties of Being Ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Also fearing that if the powerful minister truly left office the ruler's heart might easily grow lax and great power slip aside, he submitted the six admonitions entitled "The Difficulties of Being Ruler."

sentences.zh: 召為祕書郎，兼莊文府教授。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat collator, concurrently instructor in the household of Prince Zhuangwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Secretariat collator and concurrently made instructor in the household of Prince Zhuangwen.

sentences.zh: 端平初，入對，上五事，且曰：「隠蔽君徳，昔咎故相，故臣得以專詆權臣；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping he had an imperial audience, submitted five matters, and said: "When the ruler's virtue was obscured, I could blame the former chief minister, so your servant could devote himself to denouncing the powerful minister;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duanping he had an imperial audience, submitted five matters, and said, "When the ruler's virtue was obscured, I could blame the former chief minister, so your servant could devote himself to denouncing the powerful minister;

sentences.zh: 昭明君徳，今在陛下，故臣得以責難君父。

translations.literal: now that the ruler's virtue is made manifest, it lies with Your Majesty, so your servant can hold the ruler-father to account.
translations.idiomatic: now that the ruler's virtue is made manifest, it lies with Your Majesty, so your servant can hold the ruler-father to account.

sentences.zh: 乞召真徳秀、魏了翁用之。」

translations.literal: I beg that Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng be summoned and employed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng be summoned and employed."

sentences.zh: 帝謂之曰：「人主之職無他，惟辨君子小人。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "The ruler's task is nothing other than distinguishing the gentleman from the petty man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "The ruler's task is nothing other than distinguishing the gentleman from the petty man."

sentences.zh: 重珍對曰：「小人亦指君子為小人，此為難辨，人主當精擇人望，處之要津，正論日聞，則必知君子姓名，小人情狀矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongzhen replied: "Petty men also call gentlemen petty men—this is what makes it hard to distinguish. The ruler ought carefully to select men of public standing and place them in key posts; with upright discourse heard daily, one will surely know gentlemen by name and petty men by their character."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhen replied, "Petty men also call gentlemen petty men—this is what makes it hard to distinguish. The ruler ought carefully to select men of public standing and place them in key posts. With upright discourse heard daily, one will surely know gentlemen by name and petty men by their character."

sentences.zh: 兼崇政殿說書，戒家事勿以白，務積精神以寤上意，每草奏，齋心盛服，有密啟，則手書削槀，帝稱其平實。

translations.literal: Concurrently lecturer at Chongzheng Hall, he refrained from reporting family matters, strove to concentrate his spirit to awaken the emperor's intent; whenever he drafted a memorial he fasted and wore full dress; when there was a secret report he personally wrote and deleted drafts. The emperor praised his evenness and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrently lecturer at Chongzheng Hall, he refrained from reporting family matters and strove to concentrate his spirit to awaken the emperor's intent. Whenever he drafted a memorial he fasted and wore full dress; for secret reports he personally wrote and revised drafts. The emperor praised his evenness and sincerity.

sentences.zh: 遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 邉帥以《八陵圖》來上，詔百官集議，重珍言：「史嵩之既失相位，危於幕巢，猶欲邀功自固其位，請擇賢帥，如漢用充國，使之親至邉境，審度事勢，條上便宜。」

translations.literal: A frontier commander submitted the "Eight Mausoleums Map"; the court ordered all officials to assemble for deliberation. Zhongzhen said: "Shi Songzhi having lost the chancellorship is as precarious as a nest under the eaves, yet still seeks merit to secure his position. I ask that a worthy commander be chosen—as Han used Zhao Chongguo—sent in person to the frontier to assess the situation and submit recommended measures."
translations.idiomatic: A frontier commander submitted the "Eight Mausoleums Map," and the court ordered all officials to assemble for deliberation. Zhongzhen said, "Shi Songzhi having lost the chancellorship is as precarious as a nest under the eaves, yet still seeks merit to secure his position. I ask that a worthy commander be chosen—as Han used Zhao Chongguo—and sent in person to the frontier to assess the situation and submit recommended measures."

sentences.zh: 丞相主出師關洛，重珍力爭，會邉帥議和戰不一，復召集議，重珍奏：「曩乞専意備守，不得已則用應兵，今不敢變前說。」

translations.literal: The chief minister advocated sending troops to Guan and Luo; Zhongzhen argued forcefully against it. When frontier commanders disagreed on war and peace, deliberation was convened again; Zhongzhen memorialized: "I formerly asked to devote ourselves wholly to defense; if absolutely unavoidable, then use responsive troops—now I dare not change my earlier position."
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister advocated sending troops to Guan and Luo; Zhongzhen argued forcefully against it. When frontier commanders disagreed on war and peace, deliberation was convened again. Zhongzhen memorialized, "I formerly asked that we devote ourselves wholly to defense and, only if absolutely unavoidable, use responsive troops—now I dare not change my earlier position."

sentences.zh: 不聴，遂自劾以密勿清光，乃不能遏兵端，乞免說書職。

translations.literal: His counsel was not heeded; he then impeached himself—that close to the imperial brightness he had been unable to stop the opening of hostilities—and asked to be relieved of his lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was not heeded. He then impeached himself—that in confidential attendance upon the clear radiance of the throne he had been unable to stop the opening of hostilities—and asked to be relieved of his lectureship.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎，兼權司封郎官、起居舍人，言：「近者當侍講席，旋命止之，或曰是日道流生朝。

translations.literal: He was promoted to compiler, concurrently acting officer of the Ministry of Personnel's seal office and recorder of imperial action. He said: "Recently I was to attend the lecture mat, then was ordered to stop. Some say that day was the Daoist priest's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compiler, concurrently acting officer of the Ministry of Personnel's seal office and recorder of imperial action. He said, "Recently I was to attend the lecture mat, then was ordered to stop. Some say that day was a Daoist priest's birthday.

sentences.zh: 夫輟講，偶以他故，則當知聖躬舉措之難，或所傳果得其實，則當知聖心持守之難。」

translations.literal: If the lecture was suspended merely for some other reason, one should understand the difficulty of the emperor's conduct; if what is reported truly reflects the facts, then one should understand the difficulty of the emperor's self-restraint."
translations.idiomatic: If the lecture was suspended merely for some other reason, one should understand the difficulty of the emperor's conduct; if what is reported truly reflects the facts, then one should understand the difficulty of the emperor's self-restraint."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非卿，不聞此言。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "But for you, I would never have heard this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But for you, I would never have heard this."

sentences.zh: 闗洛師大衂，復進兵，重珍言：「若恥敗而欲勝之，則心不平而成忿，氣不平而成怒，生靈之命，豈可以忿怒用哉？」

translations.literal: When the Guan-Luo army suffered a great defeat and troops were sent again, Zhongzhen said: "If one is shamed by defeat and seeks victory, the heart grows unbalanced and becomes resentment, the spirit grows unbalanced and becomes rage—can the lives of the people be spent in rage?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Guan-Luo army suffered a great defeat and troops were sent again, Zhongzhen said, "If one is shamed by defeat and seeks victory, the heart grows unbalanced and becomes resentment, the spirit grows unbalanced and becomes rage—can the lives of the people be spent in rage?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「邇来用臺諫，頗主不必矯激之説，似畏剛方太過之士。

translations.literal: He also said: "Lately in employing censor-remonstrators, the prevailing view is that they need not be rigidly provocative—seemingly fearing men of excessive forthrightness and firmness.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Lately in employing censor-remonstrators, the prevailing view is that they need not be rigidly provocative—seemingly fearing men of excessive forthrightness and firmness.

sentences.zh: 竊窺選用之意，正謂其平易而省事耳！

translations.literal: Your servant has privately inferred the intent of selection: it means precisely that they should be mild and save trouble!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has privately inferred the intent of selection: it means precisely that they should be mild and save trouble!

sentences.zh: 然數月之間，一失於某，再失於某，借曰慎重臺綱，而憂其激，亦當以平正者居之。」

translations.literal: Yet within a few months one error here, another error there—even granting concern for the dignity of the censorate and fear of provocation, upright and fair men ought still to hold those posts."
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a few months one error here, another error there—even granting concern for the dignity of the censorate and fear of provocation, upright and fair men ought still to hold those posts."

sentences.zh: 又論禁旅貧弱，教習頻嚴，輙不能堪，不稍變通，非消變之道。

translations.literal: He also argued that the palace guard was poor and weak, training was frequently harsh beyond endurance, and without some flexibility this was not the way to dispel calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the palace guard was poor and weak, training was frequently harsh beyond endurance, and without some flexibility this was not the way to dispel calamity.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，言：「更化以來，舊𡚁未去者五：徇私、調停、覆護、姑息、依違是也。

translations.literal: Concurrently compiler at the National History Institute and collator at the Veritable Records Institute, he said: "Since the change of governance, five old evils remain unremoved: favoritism, mediation, covering up, indulgence, and wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrently compiler at the National History Institute and collator at the Veritable Records Institute, he said, "Since the change of governance, five old evils remain unremoved: favoritism, mediation, covering up, indulgence, and wavering.

sentences.zh: 今又益之以輕易。」

translations.literal: Now a sixth has been added—rashness."
translations.idiomatic: Now a sixth has been added—rashness."

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎，以疾求去，以集英殿修撰，知安吉州，權刑部侍郎，三辭，不許，自劾其不能取信朝廷之罪，乞鐫斥，置閒散，促覲愈力，而疾不可起，詔守刑部侍郎致仕，贈朝請大夫，謚「忠文」。

translations.literal: He was promoted to recorder of imperial action; ill, he asked to leave, was given Jiying Hall compiler, made prefect of Anji, and acting vice minister of Justice—three times he declined and was not permitted; he impeached himself for the offense of being unable to win the court's trust, begged to be branded and expelled and placed in an idle post; he pressed ever harder to attend audience, but his illness could not be overcome; an edict ordered him to retain the vice ministership of Justice in retirement, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grandee for Imperial Audience, and gave the posthumous title "Loyal and Literary."
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to recorder of imperial action. Ill, he asked to leave and was given Jiying Hall compiler, appointment as prefect of Anji, and acting vice minister of Justice. Three times he declined and was not permitted. He impeached himself for failing to win the court's trust, begged to be branded and expelled and placed in an idle post, and pressed ever harder to attend audience, but his illness could not be overcome. An edict ordered him to retain the vice ministership of Justice in retirement, posthumously honored him as Grandee for Imperial Audience, and gave the posthumous title "Loyal and Literary."

sentences.zh: 牟子才，字存容，井研人。

translations.literal: Mou Zicai, styled Cunrong, was a native of Jingyan.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Zicai, whose style name was Cunrong, came from Jingyan.

sentences.zh: 八世祖允良，生期歲，淳化間盗起，舉家殱焉，惟一姑未筓，以甕覆之得免。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Yunliang, when one full year old, during the Chunhua era bandits arose and the whole family perished; only one aunt, not yet having her hair bound, was covered with a jar and thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Yunliang was one year old when bandits rose during the Chunhua era and wiped out the entire family; only one aunt, still a girl, survived because someone covered her with a jar.

sentences.zh: 子才少從其父客陳咸，咸張樂大宴，子才閉户讀書，若不聞見者，咸異之。

translations.literal: When Zicai was young he followed his father to lodge with Chen Xian; Xian set out music and held a great banquet, while Zicai closed his door and read books as if he saw and heard nothing—Xian marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zicai accompanied his father as a guest of Chen Xian. Xian staged music and a grand feast, but Zicai shut his door and read as though he noticed nothing, which struck Xian as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 學於魏了翁、楊子謨、虞剛簡，又從李方子——方子，朱熹門人也。

translations.literal: He studied under Wei Liaoweng, Yang Zimo, and Yu Gangjian, and also followed Li Fangzi—Fangzi was a disciple of Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with Wei Liaoweng, Yang Zimo, and Yu Gangjian, and also learned from Li Fangzi, a disciple of Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十六年，舉進士，對策，詆丞相史彌逺，調嘉定府洪雅縣尉，監成都府𣙜茶司賣引所，辟四川提舉茶馬司凖備差遣，使者魏泌衆人遇之，子才拂衣竟去，泌以書幣謝，不受，改辟總領四川財賦所幹辦公事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination; in the policy disputation he criticized chief counselor Shi Miyuan. He was assigned as district captain of Hongya County in Jiading Prefecture, supervised the Chengdu prefectural tea bureau license-sale office, and was recruited as a standby emissary of the Sichuan tea-and-horse commissioner. When the envoy Wei Mi and his party met him, Zicai shook off his robe and left straightaway; Mi sent letters and gifts to apologize, but he would not accept, and instead accepted recruitment as a handler of general affairs at the Sichuan revenue and military provisions office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1223 he passed the jinshi examination and, in the policy disputation, criticized Chief Counselor Shi Miyuan. He was posted as district captain of Hongya in Jiading Prefecture, supervised the Chengdu tea license office, and was recruited as a standby emissary for the Sichuan tea-and-horse commissioner. When the envoy Wei Mi and his party met him, Zicai shook off his robe and walked away. Mi sent letters and gifts to apologize, but Zicai refused them and instead took a post handling general affairs at the Sichuan revenue and military supplies office.

sentences.zh: 詔李心傳即成都修《四朝會要》，辟兼檢閱文字。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Xinchuan to compile the Four Reigns Essentials at Chengdu, and Zicai was recruited additionally as textual reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Li Xinchuan to compile the Four Reigns Essentials at Chengdu and recruited Zicai as an additional textual reviewer.

sentences.zh: 制置司遣之文州，視王宣軍饟，鄧艾縋兵處也，道遇宣曰：「敵且壓境，宣已退矣，君無庸往。

translations.literal: The pacification commission sent him to Wenzhou to inspect Wang Xuan's army provisions—the place where Deng Ai lowered himself on ropes with troops. On the road he met Xuan, who said: "The enemy is about to press the border; Xuan has already withdrawn—there is no need for you to go.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commission sent him to Wenzhou to inspect Wang Xuan's army provisions, the very place where Deng Ai had lowered troops on ropes. On the road he met Xuan, who said: "The enemy is about to press the border. I have already withdrawn, so there is no need for you to go.

sentences.zh: 」子才不可，遂至州視軍庾而還，甫出境，文州䧟。

translations.literal: " Zicai would not accept this and went to the prefecture to inspect the military granaries before returning; he had just crossed the border when Wenzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: " Zicai refused and went on to Wenzhou to inspect the military granaries before returning. He had just left the prefecture when Wenzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 辟知成都府温江縣事，未上，連丁内外艱，時成都已破，遂盡室東下，免䘮，心傳方修《中興四朝國史》，請子才自助，擢史館檢閱。

translations.literal: Recruited to administer Wenjiang County under Chengdu Prefecture, before taking up the post he successively entered mourning for both parents. Chengdu had already fallen, so he moved his entire household eastward. Upon leaving mourning, as Xinchuan was compiling the National History of the Four Reigns of the Restoration, he asked Zicai to assist and Zicai was promoted to Historical Archive textual reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited to govern Wenjiang County under Chengdu Prefecture, but before taking office he lost both parents in succession. Chengdu had already fallen, so he moved his whole household east. After mourning, while Li Xinchuan was compiling the National History of the Four Reigns of the Restoration, he asked Zicai to assist and promoted him to Historical Archive textual reviewer.

sentences.zh: 入對，首言大臣不公不和六事，次陳備邉三策，理宗顧問甚悉，將下殿，復召與語，翼日，帝諭宰相曰：「人才如此，可峻擢之。

translations.literal: He entered audience, first speaking of six matters in which ministers were unjust and discordant, then setting forth three policies for border defense. Emperor Lizong questioned him in detail; as he was about to leave the hall he was summoned again to speak. The next day the emperor told the chief ministers: "Talent such as this should be sharply promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he first listed six ways in which ministers were unjust and disunited, then presented three policies for border defense. Emperor Lizong questioned him closely. As he was leaving the hall he was summoned back to speak again. The next day the emperor told the chief ministers: "Talent like this should be promoted sharply.

sentences.zh: 」左丞相李宗勉擬祕書郎，右丞相史嵩之怨子才言己，遽曰：「姑遷校勘。

translations.literal: Left chief counselor Li Zongmian proposed making him Secretariat Gentleman; right chief counselor Shi Songzhi, resentful that Zicai had spoken against him, hastily said: "For now let him be transferred to collation and review."
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Counselor Li Zongmian proposed appointing him Secretariat Gentleman, but Right Chief Counselor Shi Songzhi, resentful that Zicai had criticized him, quickly said: "For now transfer him to collation and review."

sentences.zh: 」俄宗勉卒，嵩之獨相，亟請外，通判吉州，轉通判衢州。

translations.literal: " Soon Zongmian died and Songzhi became sole chief counselor. Zicai quickly requested an outside post and served as administrative vice-prefect of Jizhou, then transferred to the same role in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Li Zongmian died and Shi Songzhi became sole chief counselor. Zicai quickly requested an outside post, serving as administrative vice-prefect of Jizhou and then of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 日食，詔求言，上封事萬言，極陳時政得失，且乞早定立太子。

translations.literal: A solar eclipse prompted an edict seeking advice; he submitted a sealed memorial of ten thousand characters, fully stating the gains and losses of current policy, and also begged that the heir apparent be established early.
translations.idiomatic: After a solar eclipse an edict sought advice. He submitted a sealed memorial of ten thousand characters, fully analyzing current policy and urging that the heir apparent be established soon.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監主簿兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as director of the Directorate of Education's chief clerk, concurrently serving as Historical Archive collator.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as chief clerk of the Directorate of Education, concurrently serving as Historical Archive collator.

sentences.zh: 踰年，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 鄭清之再相，子才兩上封事，言今日有徽欽時十證，又請為濟王立後，以回天怒。

translations.literal: When Zheng Qingzhi again became chief counselor, Zicai twice submitted sealed memorials, saying that the present day had ten proofs like those of the Huizong and Qinzong era, and again requesting that a successor be established for Prince Ji, to turn back Heaven's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Qingzhi again became chief counselor, Zicai twice submitted sealed memorials, saying the present age showed ten signs like those of the Huizong and Qinzong era, and again asking that an heir be established for Prince Ji to turn back Heaven's wrath.

sentences.zh: 校書郎徐霖言諫議大夫鄭宷、臨安府尹趙與𥲅，不報出關，子才言：「陛下行霖言，則霖留；

translations.literal: Proofreading Gentleman Xu Lin criticized Remonstrance Grandee Zheng Shen and Lin'an Prefecture prefect Zhao Yuze; receiving no response he left the capital. Zicai said: "If Your Majesty acts on Lin's words, then Lin will stay;
translations.idiomatic: Proofreading Gentleman Xu Lin criticized Remonstrance Grandee Zheng Shen and Lin'an Prefect Zhao Yuze. Receiving no response, he left the capital. Zicai said: "If Your Majesty acts on Lin's words, Lin will stay;

sentences.zh: 不然，則不留也。

translations.literal: otherwise he will not stay.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise he will not stay.

sentences.zh: 二人之中，宷尤無恥，請先罷之。

translations.literal: Of the two men, Shen is especially shameless—please remove him first.
translations.idiomatic: Of the two, Shen is especially shameless. Please remove him first.

sentences.zh: 」寀去。

translations.literal: " Shen left.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 至若嵩之謀復相，清之誤引嵩之之黨别之傑共政，皆歴歴為上言之。

translations.literal: As for Songzhi's scheme to return to the chief ministership and Qingzhi's mistaken introduction of Songzhi's partisan Bie Zhijie into shared governance—all were laid out in detail before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also laid out in detail before the emperor Shi Songzhi's plot to return to office and Zheng Qingzhi's mistake in bringing Songzhi's follower Bie Zhijie into government.

sentences.zh: 作書與孔光、張禹，切責清之，清之復書媿謝。

translations.literal: He wrote a letter styled after those to Kong Guang and Zhang Yu, sharply rebuking Qingzhi, and Qingzhi replied in letter with ashamed apology.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a letter modeled on those to Kong Guang and Zhang Yu, sharply rebuking Zheng Qingzhi, who replied with an ashamed apology.

sentences.zh: 謁告，還安吉州寓舍。

translations.literal: He requested leave and returned to his lodging in Anji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave and returned to his lodging in Anji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書郎，屢辭，主管崇道觀。

translations.literal: Promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, he repeatedly declined and instead supervised the Chongdao Taoist Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, he repeatedly declined and instead took charge of the Chongdao Taoist Abbey.

sentences.zh: 踰年，遷著作佐郎，又辭。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Assistant Drafting Gentleman and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Assistant Drafting Gentleman and again declined.

sentences.zh: 清之卒之明日，詔子才還朝，遷著作郎，左丞相謝方叔、右丞相吳潛交書道上意，趣行益急，乃至。

translations.literal: The day after Qingzhi died, an edict ordered Zicai back to court and promoted him to Drafting Gentleman. Left chief counselor Xie Fangshu and right chief counselor Wu Qian exchanged letters conveying the emperor's intent; the summons grew ever more urgent, and at last he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Zheng Qingzhi died, an edict recalled Zicai to court and promoted him to Drafting Gentleman. Left Chief Counselor Xie Fangshu and Right Chief Counselor Wu Qian exchanged letters conveying the emperor's wishes, and the summons grew ever more urgent until he finally arrived.

sentences.zh: 兼崇政殿說書，子才隨事奏陳，舉朝誦子才奏疏，皆曰有徳之言也。

translations.literal: Additionally lecturing at the Chongzheng Hall, Zicai memorialized on affairs as they arose. The whole court recited Zicai's memorials, all calling them words of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: As lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, he memorialized on current affairs as they arose. The whole court recited his memorials and called them words of moral weight.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，兼權禮部郎官。

translations.literal: Concurrently commissioner for compiling the National History Institute, textual reviewer of the Veritable Records Institute, and acting Ministry of Rites bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as National History compiler, Veritable Records textual reviewer, and acting Ministry of Rites bureau director.

sentences.zh: 時修《四朝史》，乃復兼史館檢討。

translations.literal: At the time they were compiling the Four Reigns History, so he again concurrently served as Historical Archive textual reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: While the Four Reigns History was being compiled, he again concurrently served as Historical Archive textual reviewer.

sentences.zh: 信州守徐謂禮奉行經界，苛急，又以脊杖比校催科，饑民嘯聚為亂，子才言於上，立罷經界，謫謂禮浙東。

translations.literal: The prefect of Xinzhou, Xu Weili, enforced the field-boundary survey with harsh urgency, also using back-cudgel beating to verify and press tax collection; hungry people gathered in uproar and rebelled. Zicai spoke to the emperor, who immediately abolished the field survey and demoted Weili to Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou Prefect Xu Weili enforced the field-boundary survey with harsh urgency and used back-cudgel beatings to verify tax collection. Hungry people rose in disorder. Zicai reported this to the throne, the survey was immediately abolished, and Xu Weili was demoted to Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 福建九郡同日大水，子才言：「今日納私謁、溺近習、勞土木、庇小人、失人心五者，皆蹈宣和之失，苟不恐懼修省，臣恐宣和京城之水將至矣。

translations.literal: Nine prefectures in Fujian flooded on the same day. Zicai said: "The five practices of today—accepting private audiences, indulging close favorites, exhausting the people with construction, shielding petty men, and losing the people's hearts—all repeat the failures of the Xuanhe era. If we do not fear, repent, and reform, this subject fears the waters of the Xuanhe capital will come again.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Fujian prefectures flooded on the same day. Zicai said: "Today's five evils—accepting private audiences, indulging close favorites, exhausting the people with construction, shielding petty men, and losing popular support—all repeat the failures of the Xuanhe era. If we do not fear, repent, and reform, I fear the floodwaters of the Xuanhe capital will come again.

sentences.zh: 燮理隂陽，大臣之事，宜諭大臣，息乖爭以召和氣，除壅蔽以通下情。

translations.literal: Harmonizing yin and yang is the business of great ministers—it is fitting to instruct the great ministers to cease discord that they may summon harmon qi, and remove obstruction that the sentiments of those below may flow through.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing yin and yang is the duty of great ministers. They should be instructed to end discord and summon harmonious qi, and to remove obstruction so the feelings of those below can reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 今遣使訪問水災，徳至渥也，願出内帑振之。

translations.literal: Now sending envoys to inquire into the flood disaster shows virtue reaching great depth; I hope funds from the inner treasury may be released to relief it.
translations.idiomatic: Sending envoys to inquire into the flood already shows great virtue. I hope funds from the inner treasury will be released for relief.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「君子難聚而易散，今聚者將散其幾有十。

translations.literal: He also said: "Worthies are hard to gather and easy to scatter; of those now gathered, the signs that they will scatter are nearly ten."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Worthies are hard to gather and easy to scatter. Of those now gathered, the signs that they will scatter are nearly ten."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「諡以勸懲，當出自朝廷，毋待其家自請。

translations.literal: He also said: "Posthumous titles for encouragement and censure should issue from the court—do not wait for the family to request them themselves."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Posthumous titles, meant to reward and punish, should come from the court and not wait until a family requests them."

sentences.zh: 」左司徐霖言諫議大夫葉大有，帝大怒，逐霖，給事中趙汝騰繳之，徙他官，汝騰即出闗，子才上疏留之，大有遂劾汝騰，子才上疏，訟汝騰誣，及大有之欺，未幾，罷大有言職。

translations.literal: " Left bureau director Xu Lin criticized Remonstrance Grandee Ye Dayou. The emperor was greatly angered and expelled Lin. Supervising Secretary Zhao Ruteng returned the edict, was transferred to another post, and Ruteng immediately left the capital. Zicai submitted a memorial to retain him. Dayou then impeached Ruteng. Zicai memorialized, defending Ruteng as slandered and exposing Dayou's deceit. Before long, Dayou was removed from his remonstrance office.
translations.idiomatic: " Left Bureau Director Xu Lin criticized Remonstrance Grandee Ye Dayou. The emperor was furious and expelled Lin. Supervising Secretary Zhao Ruteng returned the edict, was transferred elsewhere, and left the capital. Zicai memorialized to keep him. Ye Dayou then impeached Ruteng. Zicai defended Ruteng as slandered and exposed Dayou's deceit. Before long Ye Dayou was removed from his remonstrance office.

sentences.zh: 故事：早講，講讀官皆在；

translations.literal: Precedent: at the morning lecture, all lecturing and reading officials are present;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, at the morning lecture all lecturing and reading officials are present;

sentences.zh: 晩講，惟說書一員。

translations.literal: at the evening lecture, only the lecturer is present.
translations.idiomatic: at the evening lecture only the lecturer is present.

sentences.zh: 宰相懼子才言己，并晩講于早，自是不得獨對矣。

translations.literal: The chief counselor, fearing Zicai would speak of him, combined the evening lecture with the morning one—from then on Zicai could no longer have a private audience.
translations.idiomatic: The chief counselor, fearing Zicai would speak against him, combined the evening lecture with the morning one. From then on Zicai could no longer have a private audience.

sentences.zh: 遷軍器少監，御史蕭泰來劾髙斯得、徐霖，右司李伯玉言泰來所劾不當，上切責伯玉，降兩官罷，子才言：「陛下更化，召用諸賢。

translations.literal: Transferred to vice-director of the Armaments Directorate. Censor Xiao Tailai impeached Gao Side and Xu Lin. Right bureau director Li Boyu said Tailai's impeachments were inappropriate; the emperor sharply rebuked Boyu, demoted him two ranks and dismissed him. Zicai said: "Your Majesty has reformed the government and recalled worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Vice-Director of the Armaments Directorate. Censor Xiao Tailai impeached Gao Side and Xu Lin. Right Bureau Director Li Boyu said the impeachments were improper. The emperor sharply rebuked Boyu, demoted him two ranks, and dismissed him. Zicai said: "Your Majesty reformed the government and recalled worthy men.

sentences.zh: 今汝騰、斯得、霖相繼劾去，伯玉又重獲罪，善人盡矣！

translations.literal: Now Ruteng, Side, and Lin have been impeached and removed in succession, and Boyu has again received severe punishment—good men are exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: Now Ruteng, Side, and Lin have been impeached and removed in succession, and Boyu has again been severely punished. Good men are exhausted!

sentences.zh: 」除兼侍立、修注官，力辭。

translations.literal: " Appointed additionally as attendant scribe and annotations recorder, he forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: " Appointed additionally as attendant scribe and annotations recorder, he forcefully declined.

sentences.zh: 行都大火，子才應詔上封事，言甚切直。

translations.literal: A great fire broke out in the mobile capital; Zicai responded to the edict with a sealed memorial, speaking very bluntly.
translations.idiomatic: After a great fire in the mobile capital, Zicai responded to an edict with a sealed memorial that spoke very bluntly.

sentences.zh: 兼直舍人院，會泰來亦遷起居郎，恥與泰來同列，七疏力辭，上為出泰來，而子才亦請去不已，曰：「泰來既去，臣豈得獨留。

translations.literal: Additionally serving directly in the Drafting Institute, it happened that Tailai was also transferred to Gentleman Attendant-at-Accession. Ashamed to serve in the same rank, Zicai submitted seven memorials forcefully declining. The emperor removed Tailai for his sake, but Zicai also kept requesting to leave, saying: "Since Tailai has gone, how can this subject remain alone?
translations.idiomatic: While serving directly in the Drafting Institute, Tailai was also transferred to Gentleman Attendant-at-Accession. Ashamed to serve alongside him, Zicai submitted seven memorials forcefully declining. The emperor removed Tailai for his sake, but Zicai kept asking to leave, saying: "Since Tailai is gone, how can I remain alone?

sentences.zh: 」上不允，又言：「蜀當以嘉、渝、夔三城為要——欲保夔，則巴蓬之間，不可無屯以控扼之；

translations.literal: The emperor would not permit this. He again said: "Shu should take the three cities of Jia, Yu, and Kui as essential—if one wishes to hold Kui, between Ba and Peng there must be garrisons to control and block;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not allow it. Zicai again said: "Shu should treat Jia, Yu, and Kui as the three key cities. To hold Kui, there must be garrisons between Ba and Peng to control the route;

sentences.zh: 欲保渝，則利閬之間不可無屯以遏絶之；

translations.literal: if one wishes to hold Yu, between Li and Lang there must be garrisons to cut off and block;
translations.idiomatic: to hold Yu, there must be garrisons between Li and Lang to cut off the enemy;

sentences.zh: 欲守嘉，則潼遂之間不可無屯以掎角之。

translations.literal: if one wishes to defend Jia, between Tong and Su there must be garrisons to coordinate in pincer fashion.
translations.idiomatic: to defend Jia, there must be garrisons between Tong and Su to support one another.

sentences.zh: 屯，必萬人而後可。

translations.literal: Garrisons must be ten thousand strong before they suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Each garrison must reach ten thousand men before it can suffice.

sentences.zh: 」升兼侍讀。

translations.literal: " Promoted additionally to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted additionally to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 御史徐經孫劾府尹厲文翁，不報出闗，子才奏留之，文翁改知紹興府，又繳其命。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Jingsun impeached the capital prefect Li Wengwen; receiving no response he left the capital. Zicai memorialized to retain him. Wengwen was changed to prefect of Shaoxing, and Zicai again returned the order.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Jingsun impeached Capital Prefect Li Wengwen. Receiving no response, he left the capital. Zicai memorialized to keep him. Li Wengwen was reassigned to Shaoxing Prefecture, and Zicai again returned the order.

sentences.zh: 伯玉降官已逾年，舍人院不敢行詞，子才曰：「故事：文書行不過百刻，即為書行，以為叙復地。

translations.literal: Boyu had been demoted for more than a year, yet the Drafting Institute dared not issue the document. Zicai said: "Precedent: if documents are not issued within one hundred quarter-hours, one should issue them oneself, to establish ground for restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Li Boyu had been demoted for more than a year, yet the Drafting Institute dared not issue the document. Zicai said: "By precedent, if a document is not issued within one hundred quarter-hours, one should issue it oneself to establish grounds for restoration."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「謫詞皆褒語，可更之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The demotion wording is all praise—it may be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The demotion wording is all praise. It may be changed.

sentences.zh: 」子才不奉詔，丞相又道帝意，子才曰：「腕可斷，詞不可改。

translations.literal: Zicai would not obey the edict. The chief counselor again conveyed the emperor's intent. Zicai said: "My wrist may be severed, but the wording cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai would not obey the edict. The chief counselor again conveyed the emperor's intent. Zicai said: "My wrist may be cut off, but the wording cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 丞相欲改，則自改之。

translations.literal: If the chief counselor wishes to change it, let him change it himself.
translations.idiomatic: If the chief counselor wishes to change it, let him change it himself.

sentences.zh: 」乃已。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 淮東制置使賈似道以海州之捷，子才草奬諭詔，第述軍容之盛，不言其功，且語多戒敇，似道不樂。

translations.literal: Eastern Huai pacification commissioner Jia Sidao, for his victory at Haizhou, had Zicai draft the commendation edict. It merely described the army's splendor and did not mention his merit, and the language was mostly admonitory and restraining—Sidao was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: For Jia Sidao's victory at Haizhou as Eastern Huai Pacification Commissioner, Zicai drafted the commendation edict. It described only the army's splendor, said nothing of his merit, and was mostly admonitory. Sidao was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又言：「全蜀盛時，官軍七八萬人，通忠義為十四萬。

translations.literal: He also said: "At Shu's height, government troops numbered seventy or eighty thousand, and with loyalist militias the total was one hundred forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "At its height all Shu had seventy or eighty thousand government troops, or one hundred forty thousand counting loyal militias.

sentences.zh: 今官軍不過五萬而已，宜招新軍三萬，并撫慰田、楊二家，使歲以兵來助，如此則蜀猶可保；

translations.literal: Today government troops are no more than fifty thousand; one should recruit thirty thousand new troops, and also reassure the Tian and Yang families, so that each year they send troops to assist—thus Shu may still be held;
translations.idiomatic: Today government troops number no more than fifty thousand. We should recruit thirty thousand new troops and also reassure the Tian and Yang families so that each year they send troops to help. Thus Shu may still be held;

sentences.zh: 不，則不出三年，蜀必亡矣！

translations.literal: otherwise, within three years Shu will certainly perish!
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, within three years Shu will certainly be lost!

sentences.zh: 」湯漢、黄蛻召試學士院，子才發䇿，蛻譽嵩之，罷蛻正字去。

translations.literal: " Tang Han and Huang Tui were summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy; Zicai graded the essays. Tui praised Songzhi, so Tui was dismissed from his proofreader post and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang Han and Huang Tui were summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy. Zicai graded their essays. Huang Tui praised Shi Songzhi, so he was dismissed from his proofreader post and left.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎，言：「外郡以進奉易富貴，左右以土木蠱上心，小人以譁競朋比䧟君子，此天災所以數見也。

translations.literal: Transferred to Gentleman Attendant-at-Accession, he said: "Outer circuits trade tribute for wealth and rank; close attendants beguile the emperor's heart with construction; petty men through clamorous faction drag down worthies—this is why heavenly disasters appear so often.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Gentleman Attendant-at-Accession, he said: "Outer circuits trade tribute for wealth and rank, close attendants beguile the emperor's heart with construction, and petty men through clamorous faction drag down worthies. That is why heavenly disasters appear so often.

sentences.zh: 」明堂禮成，帝將幸西太乙宫欵謝，實欲遊西湖爾，子才力諫止。

translations.literal: " When the Bright Hall rites were completed, the emperor was to visit the Western Grand One Palace to offer thanks—really meaning to tour West Lake. Zicai forcefully remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Bright Hall rites were completed, the emperor planned to visit the Western Grand One Palace to offer thanks, but really intended to tour West Lake. Zicai forcefully remonstrated and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 皇子冠，面諭作樂章，禮部言：「古者，適子一醮，無樂；

translations.literal: At the crown prince's capping, the emperor personally ordered music composed. The Ministry of Rites said: "In antiquity, the primary heir had one libation without music;
translations.idiomatic: At the crown prince's capping ceremony the emperor personally ordered a celebratory hymn composed. The Ministry of Rites said: "In antiquity the primary heir received one libation without music;

sentences.zh: 庶子三醮，有樂，用樂非是。

translations.literal: a secondary son had three libations with music. Using music is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: a secondary son received three libations with music. Using music here is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 」子才言：「嫡庶之分，特以所立之地不同，非適専用醴，庶専用醮也，樂章乃學士院故事，况面諭，臣不敢不作。

translations.literal: Zicai said: "The distinction between primary and secondary sons lies solely in the place where they are established—it is not that the primary uses only sweet wine and the secondary only libation wine exclusively. Composing celebration hymns is Hanlin Academy precedent; moreover, with a personal order, this subject dares not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: Zicai said: "The distinction between primary and secondary sons lies only in where they are invested, not in the primary using only sweet wine and the secondary only libation wine. Composing celebration hymns is Hanlin Academy precedent, and with a personal order I dare not refuse."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 又言：「首蜀尾吳幾二萬里，今兩淮惟賈似道，荆蜀惟李曾伯二人而已，可為寒心。

translations.literal: He also said: "From Shu at the head to Wu at the tail is nearly twenty thousand li; today the two Huai circuits depend on Jia Sidao alone, and Jing and Shu on Li Zengbo alone—it is enough to chill the heart."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "From Shu in the west to Wu in the east is nearly twenty thousand li, yet today the two Huai circuits depend on Jia Sidao alone and Jing and Shu on Li Zengbo alone. That is enough to chill the heart."

sentences.zh: 」謂宜於合肥别立淮西制置司，江淮别立荆湖制置司，且於漣、楚、光、黄、均、房、巴、閬、緜、劒要害之郡，或築城，或増戍以守之，似道聞之怒曰：「是欲削吾地也！

translations.literal: He said one should separately establish a Western Huai pacification commission at Hefei and a Jing-Hu pacification commission in the Jiang-Huai region, and at strategic prefectures—Lian, Chu, Guang, Huang, Jun, Fang, Ba, Lang, Mian, and Jian—either build walls or increase garrisons to hold them. Sidao heard of this and said angrily: "This is trying to cut away my territory!
translations.idiomatic: He argued that a separate Western Huai pacification commission should be established at Hefei and a Jing-Hu pacification commission in the Jiang-Huai region, and that at strategic prefectures—Lian, Chu, Guang, Huang, Jun, Fang, Ba, Lang, Mian, and Jian—walls should be built or garrisons increased. When Sidao heard this he said angrily: "This is trying to cut away my territory!

sentences.zh: 」正月望，召妓入禁中，子才言：「此皆董宋臣輩壊陛下素履。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the first month, courtesans were summoned into the inner palace. Zicai said: "These are all matters in which Dong Songchen and his ilk ruin Your Majesty's long-held conduct."
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the first month, courtesans were summoned into the inner palace. Zicai said: "These are all ways in which Dong Songchen and his like corrupt Your Majesty's long-standing conduct."

sentences.zh: 」權兵部侍郎，屢辭，帝不允。

translations.literal: " Acting vice-minister of War, he repeatedly declined; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Appointed acting Vice-Minister of War, he repeatedly declined, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 升同修國史、實錄院同修撰，御史洪天錫劾宋臣、文翁及謝堂等，不報出闗，子才請行其言，文翁别與州郡，堂自請外補，宋臣自請辭内轄職，而宋臣録黄竟不至院，蓋懼子才復有言也。

translations.literal: Promoted to associate compiler of the National History and Veritable Records. Censor Hong Tiansi impeached Songchen, Wengwen, and Xie Tang and others; receiving no response he left the capital. Zicai requested that their words be acted on. Wengwen was given another prefecture, Tang requested an outside appointment, Songchen requested to resign his inner-palace post—and Songchen's recorded yellow document never reached the institute, likely fearing Zicai would again speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to associate compiler of the National History and Veritable Records, he saw Censor Hong Tiansi impeach Dong Songchen, Li Wengwen, Xie Tang, and others. Receiving no response, Hong left the capital. Zicai asked that the charges be acted on. Li Wengwen was given another prefecture, Xie Tang requested an outside post, and Dong Songchen asked to resign his inner-palace office—but Dong Songchen's recorded appointment never reached the institute, likely fearing Zicai would speak out again.

sentences.zh: 吳子聰之姑知古為女冠，得幸，子聰因之以進，得知閤門事，子才繳之曰：「子聰依憑城社，勢燄薰灼，以官爵為市，搢紳之無恥者，輻湊其門，公論素所切齒，不可用。

translations.literal: Wu Zicong's aunt Zhigu, a Daoist nun, gained favor; Zicong advanced through her and was appointed to know the Gate-Closing Affairs. Zicai returned the order, saying: "Zicong relies on patronage like rats on city walls and shrine trees; his authority blazes hot; he trades office and rank as in a market. Shameless gentry officials converge on his gate like wheel spokes. Public opinion has long gnashed teeth at him—he cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zicong's aunt Zhigu, a Daoist nun, gained imperial favor, and Zicong advanced through her to an appointment managing Gate-Closing Affairs. Zicai returned the order, saying: "Zicong relies on powerful patrons, his influence burns hot, and he trades offices and ranks like goods in a market. Shameless gentry officials flock to his door. Public opinion has long detested him. He must not be used."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「子聰之除，將一月矣，乃始繳駁，何也？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zicong's appointment was nearly a month ago—why only now return and reject it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zicong's appointment was nearly a month ago. Why do you return and reject it only now?

sentences.zh: 可即為書行。

translations.literal: Issue the document at once.
translations.idiomatic: Issue the document at once.

sentences.zh: 」子才曰：「文書不過百刻，此舊制也。

translations.literal: Zicai said: "Documents must not exceed one hundred quarter-hours—this is old regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai said: "Documents must not exceed one hundred quarter-hours. That is the old regulation.

sentences.zh: 今子聰録黄，二十餘日乃至後省，蓋欲俟其供職，使臣不得繳之耳。

translations.literal: Now Zicong's recorded yellow took more than twenty days to reach the rear secretariat—clearly intending to wait until he took office so that this subject could not return it.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong's recorded appointment took more than twenty days to reach the rear secretariat, clearly so he could take office before I could return it.

sentences.zh: 給舍，紀綱之地，豈容此輩得以行私於其間。

translations.literal: The supervising and drafting posts are where discipline lies—how can such men be allowed to practice private interests there?
translations.idiomatic: The supervising and drafting posts are where discipline is upheld. How can such men be allowed to pursue private interests there?

sentences.zh: 」於是子聰改知澧州，待次，子才力辭去，帝遣檢正姚希得挽留之，不可，以集英殿修撰，知太平州。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zicong was changed to prefect of Lizhou, awaiting his turn. Zicai forcefully declined and left. The emperor sent Rectifying Secretary Yao Xide to detain him—it was no use. He was made Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Excellence and appointed prefect of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Wu Zicong was reassigned to Lizhou Prefecture, awaiting his turn. Zicai forcefully declined and left. The emperor sent Rectifying Secretary Yao Xide to detain him, but to no avail. Zicai was made Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Excellence and appointed prefect of Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前是例兼提領江淮茶鹽，子才以不諳財懇免。

translations.literal: Previously incumbents concurrently supervised Jiang-Huai tea and salt; Zicai, unfamiliar with finance, earnestly requested exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Previously incumbents had concurrently supervised Jiang-Huai tea and salt, but Zicai, unfamiliar with finance, earnestly requested exemption.

sentences.zh: 至郡，首教民孝弟，以前人《慈竹》、《義木》二詩刻而頒之，間詣學，為諸生講說經義。

translations.literal: On reaching the prefecture, he first taught the people filial piety and brotherhood, carving and distributing two earlier poems, "Kind Bamboo" and "Righteous Tree." From time to time he visited the school to expound the classics for the students.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture he first taught the people filial piety and brotherly duty, carving and distributing two earlier poems, "Kind Bamboo" and "Righteous Tree." From time to time he visited the school to expound the classics for the students.

sentences.zh: 修采石戰艦百餘艘，造兵仗以千計。

translations.literal: He repaired over one hundred warships at Caishi and made military equipment numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired more than one hundred warships at Caishi and made military equipment numbering in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 前政負上供綱，及總所綱七十萬緡，悉為補之。

translations.literal: Previous administrations owed tribute transport quotas and seventy thousand strings in general-office quotas—all were paid by him.
translations.idiomatic: Previous administrations owed tribute transport quotas and seventy thousand strings owed to the general office—all of which he paid.

sentences.zh: 蠲黄池酒息六十餘萬貫、三縣秋苗畸零萬五千餘石、夏稅畸零紬帛四千五百餘匹、絲七百餘兩、綿一萬三千餘兩、麥二千餘石。

translations.literal: He remitted more than six hundred thousand strings of Huangchi wine interest, more than fifteen thousand odd shi of autumn grain from three counties, four thousand five hundred odd bolts of summer-tax silk fabric, more than seven hundred liang of silk thread, more than thirteen thousand liang of cotton, and more than two thousand shi of wheat.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted more than six hundred thousand strings of Huangchi wine interest, more than fifteen thousand odd shi of autumn grain from three counties, four thousand five hundred odd bolts of summer-tax silk, more than seven hundred liang of silk thread, more than thirteen thousand liang of cotton, and more than two thousand shi of wheat.

sentences.zh: 郡有平糴倉，以米五千石益之，又以緡錢二十六萬，創抵庫，歲收其息，以助糴本。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a grain-stabilization granary; he added five thousand shi of rice to it, and with two hundred sixty thousand strings created a mortgage storehouse whose annual interest supplemented the grain-purchase capital.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had a grain-stabilization granary. He added five thousand shi of rice to it and, with two hundred sixty thousand strings, created a mortgage storehouse whose annual interest supplemented the grain-purchase fund.

sentences.zh: 召入對，權工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was acting vice-minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, he was made acting Vice-Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時丁大全與宋臣表裏，濁亂朝政，子才累疏辭歸。

translations.literal: At the time Ding Daquan and Songchen worked inside and outside together, muddying and disordering court affairs. Zicai repeatedly memorialized requesting to return home.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ding Daquan and Dong Songchen worked in concert inside and outside the court, muddying government affairs. Zicai repeatedly memorialized asking to return home.

sentences.zh: 初，子才在太平建李白祠，自為記曰：「白之斥，實由髙力士，激怒妃子以報脫鞾之憾也。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Taiping Zicai built a shrine to Li Bai and wrote the inscription himself: "Bai's banishment was truly due to Gao Lishi, who inflamed the consort to avenge the grievance of having his boots removed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Taiping Zicai built a shrine to Li Bai and wrote the inscription himself: "Bai's banishment was truly due to Gao Lishi, who inflamed the consort to avenge the humiliation of having his boots removed.

sentences.zh: 力士方貴倨，豈甘以奴𨽻自處者，白非直以氣陵亢而已，蓋以為掃除之職，固當爾，所以反其極重之勢也，彼昏不知，顧為逐其所忌，力士聲勢益張，宦官之盛，遂自是始。

translations.literal: Lishi was then noble and arrogant—how could he willingly remain in servile station? Bai was not merely overbearing in spirit; he considered sweeping the floor a proper duty and therefore reversed that weightiest power. Those benighted ones did not know, and only drove away those they feared. Lishi's authority grew ever greater, and the eunuchs' ascendancy began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi was then proud and powerful—how could he willingly remain in servile station? Bai was not merely overbearing in spirit; he considered sweeping the floor a proper duty and thereby reversed that weightiest power. Those benighted men did not understand and simply drove away those they feared. Lishi's authority grew ever greater, and the eunuchs' ascendancy began from this.

sentences.zh: 其後分提禁旅，蹀血宫庭，雖天子且不得奴𨽻之矣！

translations.literal: Afterward they separately controlled the palace guard, trampling blood through the palace halls—so that even the Son of Heaven could no longer keep them in servile station!
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they separately controlled the palace guard and trampled blood through the palace halls, so that even the Son of Heaven could no longer keep them in servile station!

sentences.zh: 」又寫力士脫鞾之狀為之贊，而刻諸石，屬有拓本遺宋臣，宋臣大怒，持二碑泣愬於帝，乃與大全合謀，嗾御史交章，誣劾子才在郡公燕及餽遺過客為入已，降兩官猶未已，帝疑之，密以槧問安吉守吳子明，子明奏曰：「臣嘗至子才家，四壁蕭然，人咸知其清貧，陛下無信讒言。

translations.literal: He also wrote an inscription describing Lishi removing his boots and had it carved on stone. Someone left a rubbing with Songchen. Songchen was greatly angered, took the two steles and wept in appeal before the emperor. He then plotted with Daquan, inciting censors to submit successive memorials falsely impeaching Zicai for holding public feasts in the prefecture and keeping gifts to passing guests for himself. Zicai was demoted two ranks, yet they did not stop. The emperor doubted it and secretly sent a written query to Anji prefect Wu Ziming. Ziming memorialized: "This subject once visited Zicai's home—bare walls on four sides, amusing himself with zither and books; guests filled the seats and drinking continued till midnight. Never did this subject see a single cash enter his household."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an inscription describing Lishi removing his boots and had it carved on stone. Someone left a rubbing with Dong Songchen. Songchen was furious, took the two steles, and wept in appeal before the emperor. He then plotted with Ding Daquan and incited censors to submit successive memorials falsely accusing Zicai of holding public feasts in the prefecture and keeping gifts from passing guests for himself. Zicai was demoted two ranks, yet they did not stop. The emperor doubted this and secretly sent a written query to Anji Prefect Wu Ziming. Ziming memorialized: "I once visited Zicai's home. The walls were bare, he amused himself with zither and books, guests filled the seats, and drinking continued until midnight. I never saw a single cash enter his household."

sentences.zh: 」帝語經筵官曰：「牟子才之事，吳子明乃謂無之，何也？

translations.literal: The emperor said to the classics lecturers: "In the matter of Mou Zicai, Wu Ziming says there is nothing to it—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the classics lecturers: "In the matter of Mou Zicai, Wu Ziming says there is nothing to it. Why?"

sentences.zh: 」衆莫敢對，戴慶炣曰：「臣憶子才嘗繳子明之兄子聰。

translations.literal: None dared reply. Dai Qingke said: "This subject recalls that Zicai once returned an order against Ziming's elder brother Zicong."
translations.idiomatic: No one dared reply. Dai Qingke said: "I recall that Zicai once returned an order against Ziming's elder brother Zicong."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "So it is."

sentences.zh: 」事遂解，蓋公論所在，雖仇讐不可廢也。

translations.literal: " The matter was then resolved—public opinion had its place, and even enemies could not override it.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was then resolved, for public opinion had its place and even enemies could not override it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大全敗，宋臣斥，誣劾子才者，悉竄嶺海外，乃復子才官職，提舉玉隆萬夀宫。

translations.literal: Before long Daquan fell and Songchen was expelled. Those who had falsely impeached Zicai were all banished beyond the Ling Mountains. Zicai's offices were restored and he was made supervisor of the Yulong Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ding Daquan fell and Dong Songchen was expelled. Those who had falsely impeached Zicai were all banished beyond the Ling Mountains. Zicai's offices were restored and he was made supervisor of the Yulong Wanshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝即欲召子才，會似道入相，素憚子才，又憾草詔事，僅進實章閣待制、知温州，又嗾御史造飛語，目子才為潛黨，將中以危禍，上意不可奪，遂以禮部侍郎召，屢辭，不許，乃賜御筆曰：「朕久思見卿，故有是命，卿其勿疑，為我彊起。

translations.literal: The emperor wished at once to summon Zicai, but as Sidao entered the chief ministership—having long feared Zicai and also resenting the edict-drafting affair—he only advanced him to Pavilion Academician of the Hall for Realizing Rectitude and prefect of Wenzhou, and incited censors to fabricate slander, branding Zicai a member of Wu Qian's faction and preparing to trap him in grave peril. The emperor's intent could not be overborne; he was eventually summoned as vice-minister of Rites. Zicai repeatedly declined and was not permitted. The emperor then granted him an imperial brush-note: "We have long wished to see you, hence this appointment—do not doubt, and come early."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished at once to summon Zicai, but as Jia Sidao entered the chief ministership—having long feared Zicai and resenting the edict-drafting affair—he only advanced him to Pavilion Academician of the Hall for Realizing Rectitude and prefect of Wenzhou, and incited censors to fabricate slander branding Zicai a member of Wu Qian's faction and preparing to trap him in grave peril. The emperor's intent could not be overborne, and Zicai was eventually summoned as Vice-Minister of Rites. He repeatedly declined and was not permitted. The emperor then granted him an imperial brush-note: "I have long wished to see you, hence this appointment. Do not doubt, and come early."

sentences.zh: 」故事：近臣自外召者，必先見帝乃供職。

translations.literal: " Precedent: when a close minister is recalled from outside, he must first see the emperor before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: " By precedent, when a close minister is recalled from outside he must first see the emperor before taking office.

sentences.zh: 子才至北闗，請内引奏事，宦者在旁沮之，帝特令見，大說，慰諭久之。

translations.literal: Zicai reached the North Gate and requested an inner audience to present affairs. Eunuchs beside him discouraged it, but the emperor specially ordered him received. Greatly pleased, the emperor comforted and instructed him at length.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai reached the North Gate and requested an inner audience to present affairs. Eunuchs nearby tried to discourage it, but the emperor specially ordered him received. Greatly pleased, the emperor comforted and instructed him at length.

sentences.zh: 時似道自謂有再造功，四方無虞皆其力，故肆意逸樂，惡聞讜言，子才言：「開慶之時，天下岌岌殆矣。

translations.literal: At the time Sidao considered himself to have the merit of national restoration and that the realm's freedom from worry was all his doing, so he indulged in ease and pleasure and hated to hear blunt counsel. Zicai said: "In the Kaqing era the realm was tottering on the brink.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jia Sidao considered himself to have restored the dynasty and believed the realm's freedom from worry was all his doing, so he indulged in ease and pleasure and hated blunt counsel. Zicai said: "In the Kaqing era the realm was tottering on the brink.

sentences.zh: 今幸復安，不知天將去疾，遂無復憂耶？

translations.literal: Now, fortunately restored to peace, do we not know whether Heaven is removing the illness and we need no further worry?
translations.idiomatic: Now, fortunately restored to peace, do we not know whether Heaven is removing the illness and we need no further worry?

sentences.zh: 抑順適吾意，而基異時不可測之禍也，奈何懐宴安以鴆毒，而不明閒暇之政刑乎？

translations.literal: Or are we simply accommodating our wishes and laying foundations for unforeseeable calamity later? How can we embrace feasting and ease as poison and fail to clarify governance and punishment in this time of respite?
translations.idiomatic: Or are we simply accommodating our wishes and laying foundations for unforeseeable calamity later? How can we embrace feasting and ease as poison and fail to clarify governance and punishment in this time of respite?

sentences.zh: 忠厚者，我朝之家法也；

translations.literal: Sincerity and generosity are our dynasty's household law;
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity and generosity are our dynasty's household law;

sentences.zh: 乃者小人妨國，始用一切以戕其胍，今當反其所為，奈何愈益甚乎！

translations.literal: yet recently petty men obstructed the state and began using the 'unified' approach to mutilate its vital organs. Now we should reverse what they did—how can we make it ever worse!"
translations.idiomatic: yet recently petty men obstructed the state and began using the 'unified' approach to mutilate its vital organs. Now we should reverse what they did—how can we make it ever worse?"

sentences.zh: 」謂「宜悉取祖宗所以待士愛民，祈天永命者，循而行之。

translations.literal: He said one should "take fully what the ancestors used in treating scholars and loving the people to pray Heaven for enduring mandate, and follow it in practice.
translations.idiomatic: He said one should "take fully what the ancestors used in treating scholars and loving the people to pray Heaven for an enduring mandate, and follow it in practice.

sentences.zh: 言論者，國之元氣也，今言及乘輿，尚見優假；

translations.literal: Speech and criticism are the state's vital energy. Today when criticism touches the imperial carriage, lenience is still shown;
translations.idiomatic: Speech and criticism are the state's vital energy. Today when criticism touches the imperial carriage, lenience is still shown;

sentences.zh: 事闗廊廟，忿怒斯形。

translations.literal: when it concerns the chief ministers, anger appears at once.
translations.idiomatic: when it concerns the chief ministers, anger appears at once.

sentences.zh: 朝政之闕失，臣下之蔽蒙，何由上達乎？

translations.literal: How then can failings in court governance and the blindness of officials below reach the throne?
translations.idiomatic: How then can failings in court governance and the blindness of officials below reach the throne?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「非卿不聞此言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Had it not been for you, I would not have heard these words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Had it not been for you, I would not have heard these words."

sentences.zh: 」宣坐賜茶，問外事甚悉，子才具以田里疾苦對，帝顰蹙久之，即兼侍讀，尋兼同修國史、實録院同修撰。

translations.literal: " He ordered him seated, granted tea, and questioned him exhaustively on outside affairs. Zicai fully answered with the people's hardship in fields and villages.
