The emperor frowned long. He was immediately additionally made Reader-in-Waiting, and soon additionally associate compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered him seated, granted tea, and questioned him exhaustively on outside affairs. Zicai fully answered with the people's hardship in fields and villages. The emperor frowned for a long time. Zicai was immediately additionally made Reader-in-Waiting, and soon additionally associate compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 宋臣有内侍省押班之命，舉朝爭之不能得，子才入疏，詰朝，帝出其疏示輔臣，皆曰：「子才有憂君愛國之真，無要譽沽名之巧。

translations.literal: Songchen received an appointment as deputy squad leader of the Inner Palace Service Office; the whole court disputed it but could not prevail. Zicai entered a memorial. The next morning the emperor showed his memorial to assisting ministers, who all said: "Zicai has genuine concern for ruler and state, not the artifice of seeking praise and trading on name."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Songchen received an appointment as deputy squad leader of the Inner Palace Service Office. The whole court disputed it but could not prevail. Zicai submitted a memorial. The next morning the emperor showed it to assisting ministers, who all said: "Zicai has genuine concern for ruler and state, not the artifice of seeking praise and trading on name."

sentences.zh: 」擢權禮部尚書。

translations.literal: " Promoted to acting minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，子才為執綏官，帝問漢唐文物，占對詳贍。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall sacrifice, Zicai served as cord-holder. The emperor asked about Han and Tang ritual institutions; his impromptu answers were full and ample.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall sacrifice Zicai served as cord-holder. The emperor asked about Han and Tang ritual institutions, and his impromptu answers were full and ample.

sentences.zh: 時士大夫小迕權臣，輙竄流，子才請重者量移，輕者放還。

translations.literal: At the time when scholar-officials slightly crossed powerful ministers they were promptly banished and exiled. Zicai requested that serious cases be moderately transferred and lighter ones be released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time scholar-officials who slightly crossed powerful ministers were promptly banished and exiled. Zicai asked that serious cases be moderately transferred and lighter ones be released and returned.

sentences.zh: 兼直學士院，前是，儤直多以疾免，子才始復舊制，帝賜詩褒賞，每直，輙召對内殿，語至夜分，或就賜酒果。

translations.literal: Additionally serving directly in the Hanlin Academy—for previously, duty rotations were mostly excused on grounds of illness—Zicai restored the old system. The emperor granted poetry in praise and reward. On each duty rotation he was summoned to audience in the inner hall, talking until midnight, sometimes receiving wine and fruit on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Additionally serving directly in the Hanlin Academy—for previously duty rotations were mostly excused on grounds of illness—Zicai restored the old system. The emperor granted poetry in praise and reward. On each duty rotation he was summoned to audience in the inner hall, talking until midnight, sometimes receiving wine and fruit on the spot.

sentences.zh: 兼給事中，彗星見，應詔上封事，請罷公田，更七司法。

translations.literal: Additionally Supervising Secretary. A comet appeared; responding to an edict he submitted a sealed memorial requesting abolition of public fields and reform of the seven-circuit law.
translations.idiomatic: Additionally Supervising Secretary. When a comet appeared he responded to an edict with a sealed memorial requesting abolition of public fields and reform of the seven-circuit law.

sentences.zh: 正為尚書，力辭，不許，升修國史實錄院修撰。

translations.literal: Confirmed as minister, he forcefully declined and was not permitted. Promoted to compiler of the National History and Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Confirmed as minister, he forcefully declined and was not permitted. He was promoted to compiler of the National History and Veritable Records Institute.

sentences.zh: 徐敏子以星赦量移，似道惡其為潛所用，諷後省繳之，子才不可。

translations.literal: Xu Minzi was moderately transferred under the comet amnesty. Sidao hated that he had been used by Wu Qian and hinted the rear secretariat to return the order—Zicai would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Minzi was moderately transferred under the comet amnesty. Jia Sidao hated that he had been used by Wu Qian and hinted the rear secretariat to return the order, but Zicai would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 葉李、吕宙之等上書攻似道，似道怒欲殺之，以他事下天府獄，子才請宥之，又遺書似道，似道復書，辭甚忿，徑從天府斷遣，不復以聞，蓋懼子才再有所論駁也。

translations.literal: Ye Li, Lü Zhouzhi, and others submitted memorials attacking Sidao. Sidao angrily wished to kill them; on other charges he sent them to the capital prefecture prison. Zicai requested clemency and also sent Sidao a letter. Sidao replied with very angry words and proceeded directly to judgment and sentencing from the capital prefecture, no longer reporting upward—likely fearing Zicai would again remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li, Lü Zhouzhi, and others submitted memorials attacking Jia Sidao. Sidao angrily wished to kill them and sent them to the capital prefecture prison on other charges. Zicai requested clemency and also sent Sidao a letter. Sidao replied with very angry words and proceeded directly to judgment and sentencing from the capital prefecture, no longer reporting upward, likely fearing Zicai would remonstrate again.

sentences.zh: 度宗在東宫，雅敬子才，言必稱先生，即位，授翰林學士、知制誥，力辭不拜，請去不已，進端明殿學士，以資政殿學士致仕，卒，贈四官，官其後二人。

translations.literal: Emperor Duzong, while in the Eastern Palace, deeply respected Zicai and always called him "Master." Upon accession he was granted Hanlin academician and drafter of edicts; Zicai forcefully declined and would not accept, repeatedly requesting dismissal. He was advanced to Academic Counselor of the Hall for Bright Governance and retired as Academic Counselor of the Hall for Assisting Governance. He died; four ranks were posthumously conferred and two of his descendants were given office.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Eastern Palace, Emperor Duzong deeply respected Zicai and always called him "Master." Upon accession he was granted Hanlin academician and drafter of edicts, but Zicai forcefully declined and repeatedly asked to leave. He was advanced to Academic Counselor of the Hall for Bright Governance and retired as Academic Counselor of the Hall for Assisting Governance. He died; four ranks were posthumously conferred and two of his descendants were given office.

sentences.zh: 子才事親甚孝，弟子方客死公安，挾其柩葬安吉。

translations.literal: Zicai was very filial toward his parents. His younger brother's son Fang died while sojourning in Gong'an; Zicai carried his coffin home and buried him in Anji.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai was very filial toward his parents. His younger brother's son Fang died while sojourning in Gong'an; Zicai carried his coffin home and buried him in Anji.

sentences.zh: 女弟在眉山，抜其家于兵火，致之安吉。

translations.literal: His younger sister was in Meishan; he rescued her household from the flames of war and brought them to Anji.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister was in Meishan; he rescued her household from the flames of war and brought them to Anji.

sentences.zh: 在吉州，文天祥以童子見，即期以逺大。

translations.literal: At Jizhou, Wen Tianxiang was received as a youth student; Zicai at once marked him for great future accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: At Jizhou, Wen Tianxiang was received as a youth student, and Zicai at once marked him for great future accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 所薦士，若李芾、趙卯發、劉黻、家鉉翁，後皆為忠義士。

translations.literal: Among scholars he recommended—such as Li Fu, Zhao Maofa, Liu Fu, and Jia Xuanweng—all later became loyal and righteous men.
translations.idiomatic: Among the scholars he recommended—Li Fu, Zhao Maofa, Liu Fu, and Jia Xuanweng—all later became loyal and righteous men.

sentences.zh: 平江守吳淵籍富民田，以千餘畝遺子才，皆郤之。

translations.literal: Pingjiang prefect Wu Yuan seized rich men's fields and presented more than a thousand mu to Zicai—all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang Prefect Wu Yuan seized rich men's fields and presented more than a thousand mu to Zicai, but all were refused.

sentences.zh: 身後家無餘貲，賣金帶乃克葬。

translations.literal: After death his household had no remaining wealth; only by selling his gold belt could burial be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his household had no remaining wealth; only by selling his gold belt could burial be accomplished.

sentences.zh: 有《存齋集》、内制、外制、《四朝史槀》、奏議、經筵講義、口義故事四尚易編、春秋輪輻子》獻。

translations.literal: There were the Cunzhai Collection, inner drafts, outer drafts, Drafts of the History of Four Reigns, memorials, lectures for the classics colloquium, oral explications, precedents, a compilation on the Four Revered Books and the Changes, and the Chunqiu Lunfu zi, which were presented.
translations.idiomatic: His works included the Cunzhai Collection, inner and outer imperial drafts, Drafts of the History of Four Reigns, memorials, lectures for the classics colloquium, oral explications, precedents, a compilation on the Four Revered Books and the Changes, and the Chunqiu Lunfu zi; these were all submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朱貔孫，字興甫，浮梁人。

translations.literal: Zhu Pisun, style Xingfu, was a man of Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Pisun, style Xingfu, was from Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年進士，授臨江軍學教授。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fourth year of Chunyou; he was appointed instructor at the Linjiang Circuit school.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chunyou year 4 and was appointed instructor at the Linjiang Circuit school.

sentences.zh: 丞相史嵩之聞貔孫名，欲致之館下，以祿未及親辭。

translations.literal: Grand councilor Shi Songzhi heard Pisun's name and wished to bring him under his patronage, but because his salary had not yet reached his parents, he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Shi Songzhi, hearing of Pisun's reputation, wished to bring him into his household, but Pisun declined because his salary had not yet reached his parents.

sentences.zh: 䘮父，服除，授福州學教，授差充江東安撫司幹辦公事，制置使王埜、丘岳、馬光祖、趙與陋皆薦之。

translations.literal: His father died; when mourning ended he was appointed instructor at the Fuzhou school and specially assigned staff officer of the Jiangdong pacification commission; pacification commissioners Wang Ye, Qiu Yue, Ma Guangzu, and Zhao Yulou all recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death and the mourning period, he was made instructor at the Fuzhou school and specially assigned staff officer of the Jiangdong pacification commission; pacification commissioners Wang Ye, Qiu Yue, Ma Guangzu, and Zhao Yulou all recommended him.

sentences.zh: 丁大全在臺，勢燄熏灼，天久隂雨，貔孫貽書政府，言：「回積隂之道，去姦邪，罷手實，蠲米稅。

translations.literal: Ding Daquan was at the censorate, his power and flame scorching; Heaven long sent overcast rain. Pisun sent a letter to the government saying: 'The way to turn back accumulated yin is to remove treacherous evil, abolish household registration, and remit the rice tax.'
translations.idiomatic: While Ding Daquan held sway at the censorate and his power blazed, prolonged overcast rain fell. Pisun wrote to the government: 'The way to turn back accumulated yin is to remove treacherous men, abolish the household-registration survey, and remit the rice tax.'

sentences.zh: 」姦邪，指大全也，丞相董槐得書嘉歎。

translations.literal: 'Treacherous evil' pointed at Daquan; grand councilor Dong Huai, receiving the letter, praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: 'Treacherous evil' referred to Daquan; Grand Councilor Dong Huai, on reading the letter, praised it warmly.

sentences.zh: 主管尚書刑工部架閣文字。

translations.literal: He served as director of archival documents in the Ministries of Justice and Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of archival documents in the Ministries of Justice and Works.

sentences.zh: 宦者董宋臣寵幸用事，貔孫發策試胄子，極論宦寺專權之患，宋臣諷言者論罷之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Dong Songchen, favored and wielding power, Pisun set examination questions to test the sons of officials and argued at length on the harm of eunuch monopolization of power; Songchen prompted remonstrators to denounce him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Dong Songchen enjoyed imperial favor and wielded power. Pisun set examination questions for academy students and spoke at length against eunuch monopolization of power; Songchen had remonstrators denounce him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 光祖辟添差江東安撫司機宜文字，擢史館校勘，時大全執政，使其黨許以驟用，貔孫力拒之，且謁告歸省。

translations.literal: Guangzu summoned him as specially assigned policy secretary of the Jiangdong pacification commission and promoted him to collator in the Historiography Institute; at the time Daquan held power and had his faction promise rapid promotion, but Pisun forcefully refused and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guangzu summoned him as specially assigned policy secretary of the Jiangdong pacification commission and promoted him to collator in the Historiography Institute. Ding Daquan then held power and had his faction promise him rapid promotion, but Pisun firmly refused and asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 遷太學博士，屬帝親擢監察御史，兼崇政殿說書，首疏論大全，權姦誤國之罪，倡言學校六士之寃，又以翕聚人才，凝固人心，精擇人言，增禁旅以壯帝畿，擇良守以牧内郡，選全才以守江面，嚴舟師以防海道，因地募兵以應突至之敵，并力合勢以援必守之地。

translations.literal: He was transferred to erudite of the Imperial Academy; the emperor personally promoted him to investigating censor, concurrently lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall. His first memorial denounced Daquan for the crime of a powerful traitor misleading the state and spoke for the injustice done to the six scholars of the academy; he also set forth ten matters: gathering talent, solidifying hearts, carefully selecting remonstrance, increasing the palace guard to strengthen the imperial capital, choosing good prefects to govern inner commanderies, selecting fully capable men to hold the Yangzi front, tightening the river fleet to guard the sea routes, and recruiting troops locally to meet sudden encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Imperial Academy erudite, then personally promoted by the emperor to investigating censor and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall. His first memorial denounced Ding Daquan for the crime of a powerful traitor misleading the state and spoke for the injustice done to the six scholars of the academy. He also proposed ten measures: gather talent, steady public morale, choose remonstrance carefully, increase the palace guard to strengthen the capital, appoint capable prefects to the interior, select fully qualified men to hold the Yangzi front, tighten the river fleet to guard the sea routes, and recruit troops locally to meet sudden encirclement.

sentences.zh: 時有建議遷都四明者，貔孫亟上疏言：「鑾輿若動，則三邉之將士瓦解，而四方之盗賊蠭起，必不可。

translations.literal: At the time some proposed moving the capital to Siming; Pisun urgently submitted a memorial saying: 'If the imperial carriage moves, the generals and soldiers of the three frontiers will collapse, and bandits throughout the four directions will swarm up like bees — this absolutely must not be done.'
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed moving the capital to Siming, Pisun urgently memorialized: 'If the imperial carriage moves, troops on the three frontiers will collapse and bandits will swarm up everywhere. This must not be done.'

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 貔孫在講筵，言及宋臣撓政事，忤㫖，遷大理少卿，又遷司農少卿，兼太子右諭徳，詔許乘馬赴講。

translations.literal: Pisun, at the lecture mat, spoke of Songchen obstructing government affairs and offended the imperial will; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, then to Vice Director of the Court of Revenue, concurrently Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent; an edict permitted him to ride a horse to lectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the lecture mat Pisun spoke of Dong Songchen's interference in government and gave offense; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, then Vice Director of the Court of Revenue, with concurrent appointment as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent. An edict permitted him to ride to lectures.

sentences.zh: 貔孫諭導得體，衍說經義有闗於君道者，必委曲敷暢，隂寓警戒，太子每為之改容。

translations.literal: Pisun's instruction and guidance were appropriate; when expounding classic meanings bearing on the way of the ruler, he always unfolded them fully and smoothly, secretly embedding warnings, and the heir each time changed expression on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Pisun's instruction was always tactful. When expounding classic meanings bearing on the way of the ruler, he unfolded them fully and subtly wove in warnings; the heir's expression changed each time.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，兼權直舍人院，時大禮成，封命叢委，吏持詞頭下，每夕無慮數十，貔孫運筆如飛，夜未中已就，皆温潤典雅。

translations.literal: Concurrently compiler of the National History Institute, collator of the Veritable Records Institute, and acting holder of the Imperial Drafting Academy; at the time a great rite was completed and enfeoffment commissions piled up — clerks brought down draft headings, several tens each night without fail; Pisun moved his brush like flight and finished before midnight, all warm, smooth, and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as compiler of the National History Institute, collator of the Veritable Records Institute, and acting holder of the Imperial Drafting Academy. When a major rite was completed and enfeoffment commissions piled up, clerks delivered dozens of draft headings each night; Pisun wrote with extraordinary speed and finished before midnight, every piece warm and elegant.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，授祕書監兼太子左諭徳，改監察御史兼崇政殿說書，姓名已付外矣，尋復改命浙西。

translations.literal: His mother died; when mourning ended he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then changed to investigating censor, concurrently lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; his name had already been sent out, but soon the appointment was changed again to Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death and mourning, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then made investigating censor and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall. His name had already been sent out, but soon the appointment was changed to Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 行公田，吏並縁為姦，貔孫疏其𡚁。

translations.literal: When the public-fields policy was implemented, clerks all used it as a pretext for corruption; Pisun memorialized its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: When the public-fields policy was implemented, clerks used it as a pretext for corruption; Pisun memorialized the abuses.

sentences.zh: 推《春秋》尊王絀覇之㫖，勸帝崇仁政，用吉士，行正論，賜賚甚渥。

translations.literal: Expounding the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals to honor the king and restrain hegemons, he urged the emperor to esteem humane government, employ worthy men, and practice upright discourse; rewards and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Expounding the Spring and Autumn Annals' intent to honor the king and restrain hegemons, he urged the emperor to esteem humane government, employ worthy men, and heed upright discourse; the emperor bestowed generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 擢殿中侍御史兼侍講，請嚴京師淫聲奇服之禁，他所論苗耗役害及經理川蜀，皆當世急務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace attending censor, concurrently lecturer, and requested strict prohibition in the capital of licentious music and outlandish dress; his other discussions of seedling loss, corvée harm, and administration of Sichuan were all urgent affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to palace attending censor and lecturer, he asked for strict prohibition in the capital of licentious music and outlandish dress. His other memorials on crop loss, corvée burdens, and administration of Sichuan all addressed urgent matters of the day.

sentences.zh: 宋臣覆出，朝論紛然，貔孫因對，力斥其姦，卒奪祠。

translations.literal: Songchen reappeared, court opinion was in turmoil, and Pisun, in audience response, forcefully denounced his treachery; in the end Songchen was stripped of his temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Songchen returned to power and court opinion was in turmoil, Pisun spoke at audience and forcefully denounced his treachery; Songchen was finally stripped of his temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 升侍御史兼侍講，長星出東方，貔孫力詆外戚、内臣，及進奉羡餘失人心者，且曰：「回天心自回人心始。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attending censor, concurrently lecturer; a long comet appeared in the east, and Pisun forcefully denounced maternal kin, inner attendants, and those who sent surplus tribute and lost the people's hearts, saying: 'Turning back Heaven's heart begins with turning back the people's hearts.'
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to attending censor and lecturer, he spoke when a long comet appeared in the east, forcefully denouncing in-laws, inner attendants, and those who sent surplus tribute and alienated the people. He said, 'To turn Heaven's heart, begin by winning back the people's hearts.'

sentences.zh: 」辭㫖懇切，帝為之感動。

translations.literal: " His words were earnest and urgent in intent, and the emperor was moved by them.
translations.idiomatic: " His words were earnest and moving, and the emperor was deeply affected.

sentences.zh: 升侍讀，貔孫之再入臺，屬疆場多事，屢陳備禦之策。

translations.literal: He was promoted to reader-in-waiting; Pisun's second entry into the censorate came when the frontier was troubled, and he repeatedly set forth plans for defense and preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to reader-in-waiting, Pisun on his second entry into the censorate repeatedly proposed defense measures at a time of frontier crisis.

sentences.zh: 理宗春秋髙，倚成賈似道，似道擅命，貔孫隨事進諫，不肯阿附，至若行公田之政，屢於經筵密以告帝，似道自是深忌之，貔孫累疏求去。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong was advanced in years and relied on Jia Sidao; Sidao monopolized commands. Pisun remonstrated on each matter as it arose and would not flatter or attach himself. As for the public-fields policy, he repeatedly told the emperor in secret at the classics mat; from this Sidao deeply resented him, and Pisun repeatedly memorialized asking to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong was advanced in years and relied on Jia Sidao, who monopolized power. Pisun remonstrated on each matter and would not flatter him. On the public-fields policy he repeatedly told the emperor in secret at the classics mat; Sidao deeply resented him, and Pisun repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 理宗崩，度宗即位，擢右諫議大夫，賜紫金魚袋兼賜章服、犀帯，以疾乞辭言職，遷吏部尚書，不拜，帝以舊學故，雅欲留貔孫，使者旁午於道，而貔孫辭益力。

translations.literal: Lizong died and Duzong took the throne; Pisun was promoted to Right Remonstrance Counselor, granted a purple-gold fish bag together with ceremonial robes and a rhinoceros-horn belt. Citing illness he asked to resign his remonstrance post and was transferred to Minister of Personnel, but did not accept. Because of their old teacher-student relation the emperor greatly wished to keep Pisun; envoys crowded the roads, yet Pisun declined all the more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: After Lizong died and Duzong succeeded, Pisun was promoted to Right Remonstrance Counselor and granted a purple-gold fish bag, ceremonial robes, and a rhinoceros-horn belt. Citing illness he asked to leave remonstrance office and was named Minister of Personnel, but declined. Because of their old teacher-student relation the emperor greatly wished to keep him; envoys crowded the roads, yet Pisun declined ever more firmly.

sentences.zh: 以華文閣學士，知寧國府，似道諷言者論罷，久之，提舉太平興國宫，復華文閣學士、知袁州，至郡宣布徳意，以戢暴禁貪為先務，郡倉受租，舊倚斛面取贏，吏加漁取，貔孫知其𡚁，悉榜除之，許民自槩量，宿𡚁頓革，田里歡聲。

translations.literal: As Huawen Pavilion academician he was made prefect of Ningguo; Sidao prompted remonstrators to denounce him and he was dismissed. After a long while he was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, then again Huawen Pavilion academician and prefect of Yuanzhou. Reaching the prefecture he proclaimed virtuous intent and made suppressing violence and forbidding greed his first tasks. The prefectural granary, in receiving rent, had relied on surplus taken from the measure face, and clerks added further exactions; Pisun knew these abuses, posted notices abolishing them all, and permitted the people to measure for themselves; long-standing abuses were suddenly reformed and field rent suddenly increased.
translations.idiomatic: As Huawen Pavilion academician he served as prefect of Ningguo until Jia Sidao had remonstrators denounce him and he was dismissed. Long afterward he became superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, then again Huawen Pavilion academician and prefect of Yuanzhou. On reaching the prefecture he proclaimed humane intent and made suppressing violence and forbidding greed his first priorities. The prefectural granary had long taken surplus from the measure face and clerks had added further exactions; Pisun posted notices abolishing all such abuses and allowed the people to measure grain themselves. Long-standing abuses were suddenly reformed and field rent rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 興學校以勸士。

translations.literal: He established schools to encourage scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He established schools to encourage learning.

sentences.zh: 升敷文閣學士、知福州、福建安撫使，未㡬，卒于袁之郡治，贈四官，與恩澤，並令所在給䘮事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Fuwén Pavilion academician, prefect of Fuzhou, and Fujian pacification commissioner; before long he died at the Yuanzhou prefectural seat, was posthumously granted four ranks, given favor and grace, and ordered that funeral arrangements be supplied wherever he was.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Fuwén Pavilion academician, prefect of Fuzhou, and Fujian pacification commissioner, he died at the Yuanzhou prefectural seat before taking up the new posts. He was posthumously granted four ranks, given imperial favor, and orders were issued to provide funeral arrangements locally.

sentences.zh: 有文集、奏議行世。

translations.literal: He had collected writings and memorials circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings and memorials circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 歐陽守道，字公權，一字迂父，吉州人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Shoudao, style Gongquan, with another style Yufu, was a man of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Shoudao, style Gongquan, also styled Yufu, was from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 初名巽，自以更名應舉，非是當祭必稱巽。

translations.literal: His original name was Xun; he considered changing his name to take the examinations improper, and whenever sacrifice was due he always called himself Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Xun. He considered it wrong to change his name in order to take the examinations, and whenever sacrifice was due he always used the name Xun.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，無師，自力於學，里人聘為子弟師，主人瞷其每食舍肉，密歸遺母，為設二器馳送，乃肯食肉，隣媪兒無不歎息感動。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor, without a teacher; he studied by his own effort. Neighbors hired him as teacher for their sons. The master noticed that at each meal he set aside meat and secretly returned home to give it to his mother; the master set out two vessels and sent them swiftly, and only then would he eat meat. Neighboring old women and children all sighed and were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he had no teacher and studied on his own. Neighbors hired him to teach their sons. His employer noticed that at each meal he set aside meat and secretly took it home to his mother; the employer prepared two vessels and sent them quickly, and only then would he eat meat. Neighboring women and children were all moved to sigh.

sentences.zh: 年未三十，翕然以徳行為鄉郡儒宗。

translations.literal: Before age thirty he had already become, with one accord, the Confucian exemplar of his home commandery in virtue and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was thirty he was already widely regarded as the moral exemplar of Confucian learning in his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 江萬里守吉州，守道適貢于鄉，萬里獨異視之。

translations.literal: Jiang Wanli was prefect of Jizhou; Shoudao happened to submit tribute at the local examination, and Wanli alone regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wanli was prefect of Jizhou, Shoudao happened to compete in the local examination, and Wanli singled him out for special regard.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，舉進士，廷對，言：「國事成敗在宰相，人才消長在臺諫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou he passed the jinshi examination; at the palace examination he said: 'The success or failure of state affairs lies with the grand councilor; the waxing and waning of talent lies with the censorate and remonstrance officials.'
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou year 1 he passed the jinshi examination. At the palace examination he said, 'Whether state affairs succeed or fail depends on the grand councilor; whether talent rises or falls depends on the censorate and remonstrance officials.'

sentences.zh: 昔者當國惡箴規，言者疑觸迕，及其去位，共謂非才。

translations.literal: Formerly, when one held the state he hated admonition; remonstrators feared giving offense; when he left office, all said he lacked talent.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when a man held power he hated admonition and remonstrators feared giving offense; once he left office, everyone said he lacked talent.

sentences.zh: 或有迎合時宰，自效殷勤，亦有疾惡乖方，苟求疵纇，以致忠邪不辨，黜陟無章。

translations.literal: Some would cater to the chief minister and offer eager service; others, hating evil yet perverse in method, would seek flaws indiscriminately, so that loyal and treacherous were not distinguished and promotion and dismissal had no rule.
translations.idiomatic: Some would cater to the chief minister and offer eager service; others, though hating evil, were perverse in method and sought flaws indiscriminately, so that loyal and treacherous men could not be distinguished and promotion and dismissal had no rule.

sentences.zh: 」唱名，徐儼夫為第一，儼夫握守道，起曰：「吾愧出君上矣。

translations.literal: When the names were announced, Xu Yanfu was first; Yanfu grasped Shoudao's hand, rose, and said: 'I am ashamed to rank above you.'
translations.idiomatic: When the names were read aloud, Xu Yanfu ranked first. Yanfu took Shoudao's hand, rose, and said, 'I am ashamed to rank above you.'

sentences.zh: 君文未嘗不在我上也。

translations.literal: 'Your writing has never been below mine.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Your writing has never been beneath mine.'

sentences.zh: 」授雩都主簿。

translations.literal: " He was appointed chief clerk of Yudu.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed chief clerk of Yudu.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，調贑州司户。

translations.literal: His mother died; when mourning ended he was assigned as revenue officer of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death and mourning, he was assigned revenue officer of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 其次十年後，萬里作白鷺洲書院，首致守道為諸生講說。

translations.literal: About ten years later Wanli established the Bailuzhou Academy and first invited Shoudao to lecture the students.
translations.idiomatic: About ten years later Jiang Wanli established the Bailuzhou Academy and first invited Shoudao to lecture the students.

sentences.zh: 湖南轉運副使吳子良聘守道為嶽麓書院副山長，守道初升講，發明孟氏「正人心，承三聖」之說，學者悅服。

translations.literal: Hunan transport vice commissioner Wu Ziliang engaged Shoudao as associate headmaster of the Yuelu Academy; when Shoudao first ascended to lecture he expounded Mencius's saying 'rectify the human heart and inherit the three sages,' and the scholars were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan transport vice commissioner Wu Ziliang engaged Shoudao as associate headmaster of the Yuelu Academy. At his first lecture Shoudao expounded Mencius's teaching to 'rectify the human heart and inherit the three sages,' and the scholars were delighted.

sentences.zh: 宗人新及子必泰，先寓居長沙，聞守道至，往訪之，初猶未識也，晤語相契，守道即請於子良，禮新為嶽麓書院講書，新講《禮記》「天降時雨，山川出雲」一章，守道起曰：「長沙自有仲齊，吾何為至此？

translations.literal: His clansman Xin and Xin's son Bitai had earlier lived in Changsha; hearing Shoudao had arrived, they went to visit him. At first they did not yet know each other, but in conversation they were compatible. Shoudao at once asked Ziliang to honor Xin as lecturer at the Yuelu Academy. Xin lectured on the Record of Rites passage 'Heaven sends timely rain; mountains and rivers send forth clouds.' Shoudao rose and said: 'Changsha already has Zhongqi — why have I come here?'
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xin and Xin's son Bitai had been living in Changsha. Hearing Shoudao had arrived, they visited him. Though they did not yet know each other, conversation revealed a deep affinity. Shoudao at once asked Ziliang to appoint Xin lecturer at the Yuelu Academy. When Xin lectured on the Record of Rites passage 'Heaven sends timely rain; mountains and rivers send forth clouds,' Shoudao rose and said, 'Changsha already has Zhongqi — why have I come here?'

sentences.zh: 」仲齊，新之字也。

translations.literal: " Zhongqi was Xin's style.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongqi was Xin's style.

sentences.zh: 踰年，新卒，守道哭之慟，自銘其墓，又薦其子必泰於當道。

translations.literal: After a year Xin died; Shoudao wept for him in deep grief, himself composed the epitaph for his tomb, and again recommended his son Bitai to those in power.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Xin died. Shoudao mourned him deeply, wrote the tomb inscription himself, and recommended his son Bitai to those in power.

sentences.zh: 子良代，守道復還吉州，里有張基，䘮其父，小祥，而舅氏訟以事，繫之獄，使不得祭，邀其售已地以葬，守道聞之，歎曰：「吾惟痛斯子之不得一哭其父也，且其痛奈何！

translations.literal: When Ziliang was replaced, Shoudao returned again to Jizhou. In the village was Zhang Ji, who had mourned his father and reached the small mourning period, but his maternal uncle sued him over a matter, bound him in prison so he could not sacrifice, and demanded he sell his land for burial. Hearing this, Shoudao sighed and said: 'I only grieve that this son cannot weep once for his father — and how great that grief must be!'
translations.idiomatic: When Ziliang was replaced, Shoudao returned to Jizhou. In the village Zhang Ji, in mourning for his father and at the small mourning period, was sued by his maternal uncle, imprisoned so he could not sacrifice, and pressed to sell his land for burial. Shoudao sighed, 'I grieve only that this son cannot weep once for his father — and how great that grief must be!'

sentences.zh: 」明日，告之邑令，曰：「此非人心，濱祭而縛之，撓𦵏而奪之，舅如此，是自食其肉也，請任斯子出祭而復獄。

translations.literal: The next day he told the district magistrate, saying: 'This is not the human heart — on the eve of sacrifice to bind him, to disturb the coffin and seize it; for an uncle to act thus is to eat his own flesh. I ask to guarantee this son's release to sacrifice and then return to prison.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the district magistrate, 'This is inhuman — to bind a man on the eve of sacrifice, to disturb the coffin and seize it. For an uncle to act thus is to devour his own flesh. I ask to guarantee this son's release to sacrifice and then return to prison.'

sentences.zh: 」令亟出之，其舅醜誣守道，守道亦不自辨。

translations.literal: " The magistrate quickly released him; the uncle slanderously accused Shoudao, and Shoudao also did not defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: " The magistrate quickly released him. The uncle slanderously accused Shoudao, who made no defense.

sentences.zh: 轉運使包恢為請祠于朝，萬里入為國子祭酒，薦為史館檢閲，召試館職，授祕書省正字。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Bao Hui requested a temple sinecure for him at court; Wanli entered service as Director of the Directorate of Education and recommended him as collator in the Historiography Institute; he was summoned to examination for archive posts and appointed rectifier of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Bao Hui requested a temple sinecure for him at court. Jiang Wanli, after entering service as Director of the Directorate of Education, recommended him as collator in the Historiography Institute. He passed the archive examination and was appointed Secretariat rectifier.

sentences.zh: 安南國王陳日照傳位其子，求封太上國王，下省官議，守道謂：「太上者，漢髙帝以尊其父，累朝未之有改。

translations.literal: The king of Annam, Chen Riyao, transmitted the throne to his son and requested enfeoffment as Grand Senior King; the matter was sent down to provincial officials for discussion. Shoudao said: 'Grand Senior — Emperor Gaodi of Han used it to honor his father, and successive dynasties have not changed it.'
translations.idiomatic: When the king of Annam, Chen Riyao, abdicated in favor of his son and asked to be enfeoffed as Grand Senior King, the matter was referred to provincial officials for discussion. Shoudao said, 'Grand Senior — Emperor Gaodi of Han used it to honor his father, and successive dynasties have not changed the usage.'

sentences.zh: 若賜詔書，稱太上國王，非便。

translations.literal: 'If an edict is granted calling him Grand Senior King, it is not convenient.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If an edict calls him Grand Senior King, that would be inappropriate.'

sentences.zh: 南越尉佗嘗自稱蠻夷大長老，正南夷事也。

translations.literal: 'The Nan Yue commander Zhao Tuo once styled himself Great Elder of the barbarian Yi — that is the proper way to handle southern barbarian affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Nan Yue commander Zhao Tuo once styled himself Great Elder of the barbarian Yi — that is the proper way to handle southern barbarian affairs.'

sentences.zh: 《禮》方伯自稱曰天子之老，大夫致仕曰老，自稱亦曰老；

translations.literal: 'The Rites say a regional lord calls himself the Son of Heaven's elder; a grandee who retires is called elder, and in self-reference also says elder;'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Rites say a regional lord calls himself the Son of Heaven's elder; a retired grandee is called elder, and in self-reference also uses elder;'

sentences.zh: 自夷蠻言之，則有尉佗之故事，自中國言之，亦方伯致仕者之常稱。

translations.literal: 'Speaking from the barbarian Yi perspective, there is Zhao Tuo's precedent; speaking from the Central Kingdom perspective, it is also the usual title for a regional lord who has retired from office.'
translations.idiomatic: 'From the barbarian perspective there is Zhao Tuo's precedent; from the Central Kingdom perspective it is also the usual title for a retired regional lord.'

sentences.zh: 漢亦有老上單于之號，易『太』以『老』，無損，或去上字存其太字，太王則有古公三太、三少、太宰、少宰，太所以别於少也。

translations.literal: 'Han also had the title Old Upper Chanyu; changing "Grand" to "Old" does no harm. Or one may remove the character "upper" and keep "Grand"; Grand King has the precedent of the Three Grand and Three Junior of Old Duke, Grand Steward and Junior Steward — "Grand" distinguishes from "Junior."'
translations.idiomatic: 'Han also had the title Old Upper Chanyu; substituting "Old" for "Grand" would do no harm. Or one might drop "upper" and keep "Grand"; Grand King recalls the Three Grand and Three Junior of Old Duke, Grand Steward and Junior Steward — "Grand" distinguishes from "Junior."'

sentences.zh: 謂父為太，則子為少矣。

translations.literal: 'If the father is called Grand, then the son is Junior.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If the father is called Grand, then the son is Junior.'

sentences.zh: 太以尊言，則太后、太妃、太子、太孫，以卑言，則太史、太卜、太祝、樂太師、太圉，上下所通用也。

translations.literal: 'Where "Grand" speaks of honor, there are the Grand Empress Dowager, Grand Consort, Heir Apparent, and Grandson; where it speaks of low rank, there are the Grand Scribe, Grand Diviner, Grand Invoker, Music Grand Master, and Grand Stable Master — both high and low use it in common.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Where "Grand" denotes honor, there are the Grand Empress Dowager, Grand Consort, Heir Apparent, and Grandson; where it denotes lower rank, there are the Grand Scribe, Grand Diviner, Grand Invoker, Music Grand Master, and Grand Stable Master — the term is used at every level.'

sentences.zh: 」時病足不及與議，遷校書郎兼景憲府教授，遷祕書郎。

translations.literal: " At the time his feet were ill and he could not join the discussion; he was transferred to collator, concurrently instructor of the Jingxian Palace, then to Secretariat secretary.
translations.idiomatic: " His feet were ill and he could not join the discussion. He was transferred to collator and instructor of the Jingxian Palace, then to Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 轉對，言：「欲家給人足，必使中外臣庶無復前日言利之風，而後可風化，惟反諸身化之以儉，而彼不為儉，吾惟有卑宫室、菲飲食化之以㢘，而彼不興㢘，吾惟有不貴難得之貨，不厚無益之蔵。

translations.literal: At rotation audience he said: 'To wish that every household has enough requires that inside and outside, officials and commoners, no longer have the former wind of speaking of profit — only then can there be transformation through mores. One can only transform oneself by frugality; if they are not frugal, I have only to transform them by low palace chambers and plain food and drink into frugality. If they do not rise in frugality, I have only not to prize hard-to-obtain goods and not to store up what is without benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: At rotation audience he said, 'For every household to have enough, officials and commoners at court and in the provinces must abandon the old habit of talking profit — only then can mores be transformed. One must begin by transforming oneself through frugality; if others are not frugal, one can only teach frugality through modest dwellings and plain food. If they still do not embrace frugality, one must refuse to prize rare goods and refuse to hoard what does no good.'

sentences.zh: 」以言罷，守道徒步出錢塘門，唯書兩箧而已。

translations.literal: " He was dismissed on account of his words; Shoudao walked out through the Qiantang Gate with only two boxes of books.
translations.idiomatic: " Dismissed for his words, Shoudao walked out through the Qiantang Gate with only two boxes of books.

sentences.zh: 理宗遺詔聞，守道與其徒相嚮哭踊，僮奴、孺子各為悲哀。

translations.literal: When Lizong's death edict was heard, Shoudao and his disciples wept and stamped toward one another; servants and children each mourned.
translations.idiomatic: When Lizong's death edict was announced, Shoudao and his disciples wept and stamped in grief toward one another; servants and children all mourned.

sentences.zh: 咸淳三年，特㫖與祠，詔大臣舉賢才，少傅吕文徳舉九十六人，守道預焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianchun he was specially ordered granted a temple sinecure; an edict had grand ministers recommend worthy talent, and Junior Mentor Lü Wende recommended ninety-six men, Shoudao among them.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun year 3 he was specially granted a temple sinecure. When an edict ordered grand ministers to recommend worthy talent, Junior Mentor Lü Wende recommended ninety-six men, Shoudao among them.

sentences.zh: 添差通判建昌軍，以書謝廟堂，曰：「史贊大將軍不薦士，今大將軍薦士矣。

translations.literal: Specially assigned vice prefect of Jianchang Circuit, he wrote to thank the council chamber, saying: 'Shi Zan the Great General did not recommend scholars; now the Great General recommends scholars.'
translations.idiomatic: As specially assigned vice prefect of Jianchang Circuit, he wrote to thank the council chamber: 'Shi Zan the Great General did not recommend scholars — yet now the Great General recommends scholars.'

sentences.zh: 而某何以得此於大將軍哉？

translations.literal: 'By what means have I obtained this from the Great General?'
translations.idiomatic: 'How have I earned this from the Great General?'

sentences.zh: 幸嘗蒙召擢，備數三館，異時，或者謂其放廢無聊，託身諸貴人，虧傷國體，則寧得而解，願仍賦祠祿足矣。

translations.literal: 'Fortunately I was once summoned and promoted and counted among the Three Institutes. If later someone should say I was cast aside in idleness and attached myself to various powerful men, injuring the dignity of the state, then I would rather be able to explain myself; I wish only to continue receiving my temple stipend — that is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I was once summoned and promoted and counted among the Three Institutes. If later someone should say I was cast aside in idleness and attached myself to powerful men, injuring the dignity of the state, I would rather be able to explain myself. I ask only to continue receiving my temple stipend — that is enough.'

sentences.zh: 」遷著作佐郎兼崇政殿說書，兼權都官郎官，經筵所進，皆切於當世務，上為動色。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to assistant compiler, concurrently lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, concurrently acting officer of the Ministry of Punishments; what he presented at the classics mat all bore on urgent affairs of the age, and the emperor changed expression on his account.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made assistant compiler, lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, and acting officer of the Ministry of Punishments. What he presented at the classics mat all bore on urgent affairs of the day, and the emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 卒，家無一錢。

translations.literal: He died; the household had not a single coin.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving not a single coin in the house.

sentences.zh: 守道之兄之妻蚤䘮，其子演五歲餘，且多病，浚生甫數月，守道三十未有室，顧無能乳哺者，日夜抱二子泣，里巷憐之，演既長，出莫知所之，守道哭而求諸野，終不能得，三年不食肉，顦顇不釋者終身。

translations.literal: Shoudao's elder brother's wife died early; her son Yan was a little over five years and often ill; Jun was born only a few months old. Shoudao, not yet thirty and without a wife, looked about and found no one able to nurse them; day and night he held the two children and wept, and the lanes and alleys pitied him. When Yan grew up he went out and no one knew where; Shoudao wept and sought him in the wilds but never found him. For three years he ate no meat, and gauntness he never cast off all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Shoudao's elder brother's wife died young. Her son Yan was a little over five and often ill; Jun was only a few months old. Shoudao, not yet thirty and unmarried, found no one to nurse them and day and night held the two children and wept; neighbors pitied him. When Yan grew up he went out and was never seen again. Shoudao wept and searched the countryside but never found him. For three years he ate no meat, and he remained gaunt for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 吉有賢守，而大家怨之，厚誣以贓者，下其事常平使者，㑹旱甚，禱雲騰，守道曰：「無以禱也。

translations.literal: In Ji there was a worthy prefect whom powerful families resented; they heavily slandered him with charges of corruption and the matter was sent down to the Ever-Normal intendant. A severe drought coincided; prayers were offered at Yunteng. Shoudao said: 'There is no use in praying.'
translations.idiomatic: In Ji there was a worthy prefect whom powerful families resented; they heavily slandered him with corruption charges and the case was referred to the Ever-Normal intendant. During a severe drought prayers were offered at Yunteng. Shoudao said, 'Prayer will do no good.'

sentences.zh: 雲騰之神，唐郡守吳侯也。

translations.literal: 'The spirit of Yunteng is Wu Hou, prefect of the Tang dynasty.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The spirit of Yunteng is Wu Hou, a Tang prefect.'

sentences.zh: 寃莫甚於前守，寃不直而吳侯於禱，侯有辭矣。

translations.literal: 'No wrong is greater than that of the former prefect; if the wrong is not righted and Wu Hou is asked in prayer, the Marquis has grounds to refuse.'
translations.idiomatic: 'No wrong is greater than that done to the former prefect. If the wrong is not righted and Wu Hou is asked in prayer, the Marquis has grounds to refuse.'

sentences.zh: 匹婦藏寃，旱或三年，寃在民牧，害豈其小。

translations.literal: 'When a single woman harbors a wrong, drought may last three years; when the wrong lies with the people's shepherd, can the harm be small?'
translations.idiomatic: 'When a single woman harbors a wrong, drought may last three years. When the wrong lies with the people's shepherd, can the harm be small?'

sentences.zh: 」反覆千餘言，或迂笑之，守道不改，告來者不倦，守卒以得直。

translations.literal: " He repeated this in more than a thousand words; some laughed at him as pedantic, but Shoudao did not change; he told those who came without tiring, and the prefect was finally vindicated.
translations.idiomatic: " He repeated this at length in more than a thousand words. Some laughed at him as pedantic, but Shoudao did not waver. He told all who came without tiring, and the prefect was finally vindicated.

sentences.zh: 所著有易故文集。

translations.literal: Works he authored include the Yigu Collected Writings.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include the Yigu Collected Writings.

sentences.zh: 論曰：湯璹立朝蹇諤，蔣重珍自擢巍科，既居盛名之下而能樹立於當世，可為難矣！

translations.literal: The judgment says: Tang Shu stood at court with upright remonstrance; Jiang Zhongzhen, from his own elevation in the highest examination, though beneath great fame was yet able to establish himself in the age — this may be called difficult!
translations.idiomatic: The judgment says: Tang Shu stood at court with upright remonstrance; Jiang Zhongzhen, though placed beneath great fame after ranking first in the examinations, was yet able to establish himself in his age — no small achievement!

sentences.zh: 牟子才、朱貔孫直聲著於中外。

translations.literal: Mou Zicai and Zhu Pisun had straight reputations renowned inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Zicai and Zhu Pisun won renown at home and abroad for their blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 歐陽守道，廬陵之醇儒也。

translations.literal: Ouyang Shoudao was the pure Confucian of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Shoudao was the pure Confucian of Luling.
